        var decisions = PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluateAll(Subjects.Active("*"), PageTree.Standard().Pages);

        Assert.All(decisions, d => Assert.True(d.IsAllowed));
    }

    // ---- Denials, each with the right reason ----

    [Fact]
    public void Page_is_denied_when_no_grant_covers_its_permission()
    {
        var decision = Decide(Subjects.Active("reports.view"), PageTree.Standard(), "/reports/finance");

        Assert.False(decision.IsAllowed);
        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.MissingPermission, decision.Reason);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Explicit_deny_beats_a_role_grant()
    {
        var subject = Subjects.ActiveWithDenies(
            granted: ["reports.view", "reports.finance", "reports.finance.*"],
            denied: ["reports.finance.export"]);

        Assert.True(Decide(subject, PageTree.Standard(), "/reports/finance").IsAllowed);
        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.ExplicitlyDenied, Decide(subject, PageTree.Standard(), "/reports/finance/export").Reason);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Wildcard_deny_beats_a_concrete_grant()
    {
        var subject = Subjects.ActiveWithDenies(granted: ["reports.view", "reports.finance"], denied: ["reports.*"]);

        // reports.* covers reports.view too, so the deny bites at the top of
        // the branch and everything beneath it follows.
        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.ExplicitlyDenied, Decide(subject, PageTree.Standard(), "/reports").Reason);
        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.ParentDenied, Decide(subject, PageTree.Standard(), "/reports/finance").Reason);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Child_is_denied_when_its_parent_is_denied_even_if_the_child_permission_is_held()
    {
        // Holds the finance permission but not reports.view.
        var decision = Decide(Subjects.Active("reports.finance"), PageTree.Standard(), "/reports/finance");

        Assert.False(decision.IsAllowed);
        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.ParentDenied, decision.Reason);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Denial_propagates_down_every_level()
    {
        var decision = Decide(Subjects.Active("reports.finance", "reports.finance.export"), PageTree.Standard(), "/reports/finance/export");

        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.ParentDenied, decision.Reason);
    }

    // ---- Who is asking ----

    [Fact]
    public void Anonymous_subject_sees_public_pages_only()
    {
        var decisions = PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluateAll(AccessSubject.Anonymous, PageTree.Standard().Pages);

        var allowed = decisions.Where(d => d.IsAllowed).Select(d => d.Page.Path);
        Assert.Equal(["/help"], allowed);
        Assert.All(decisions.Where(d => !d.IsAllowed), d => Assert.Equal(AccessReason.NotAuthenticated, d.Reason));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Suspended_subject_loses_everything_but_public_pages_whatever_they_were_granted()
    {
        var decisions = PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluateAll(Subjects.Suspended("*"), PageTree.Standard().Pages);

        Assert.Equal(["/help"], decisions.Where(d => d.IsAllowed).Select(d => d.Page.Path));
        Assert.All(decisions.Where(d => !d.IsAllowed), d => Assert.Equal(AccessReason.UserSuspended, d.Reason));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Public_page_under_a_denied_parent_is_still_allowed()
    {
        var tree = PageTree.Standard().Add("/reports/glossary", "/reports", isPublic: true);

        var decision = Decide(AccessSubject.Anonymous, tree, "/reports/glossary");

        Assert.True(decision.IsAllowed);
        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.PublicPage, decision.Reason);
    }

    // ---- Bad data: fail closed, never throw ----

    [Fact]
    public void Orphaned_page_is_denied()
    {
        var orphan = Page.Create("/lost", "Lost", parentId: Guid.NewGuid()).Value;

        var decision = PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluateAll(Subjects.Active("*"), [orphan]).Single();

        Assert.False(decision.IsAllowed);
        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.OrphanedPage, decision.Reason);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Pages_on_a_parent_cycle_are_denied_and_pages_below_it_are_denied_as_children()
    {
        var a = Page.Create("/a", "A").Value;
        var b = Page.Create("/b", "B", parentId: a.Id).Value;
        var c = Page.Create("/c", "C", parentId: b.Id).Value;
        a.MoveUnder(b.Id); // a -> b -> a

        var decisions = PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluateAll(Subjects.Active("*"), [a, b, c])
            .ToDictionary(d => d.Page.Path, d => d.Reason);

        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.CyclicHierarchy, decisions["/a"]);
        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.CyclicHierarchy, decisions["/b"]);
        Assert.Equal(AccessReason.ParentDenied, decisions["/c"]);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void A_page_cannot_be_made_its_own_parent()
    {
        var page = Page.Create("/a", "A").Value;

        Assert.True(page.MoveUnder(page.Id).IsFailure);
        Assert.Null(page.ParentId);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Duplicate_page_ids_are_a_programming_error()
    {
        var page = Page.Create("/a", "A").Value;

        Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluateAll(Subjects.Active(), [page, page]));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void A_very_deep_tree_does_not_overflow_the_stack()
    {
        var tree = new PageTree().Add("/l0");
        for (var i = 1; i < 2_000; i++)
            tree.Add($"/l{i}", $"/l{i - 1}");

        var decisions = PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluateAll(Subjects.Active(), tree.Pages);

        Assert.Equal(2_000, decisions.Count);
        Assert.All(decisions, d => Assert.True(d.IsAllowed));
    }

    // ---- The API's contract ----

    [Fact]
    public void EvaluateAll_returns_one_decision_per_page_in_input_order()
    {
        var pages = PageTree.Standard().Pages.Reverse().ToList();

        var decisions = PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluateAll(Subjects.Active(), pages);

        Assert.Equal(pages.Select(p => p.Id), decisions.Select(d => d.Page.Id));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void EvaluateAll_with_no_pages_returns_nothing()
    {
        Assert.Empty(PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluateAll(Subjects.Active("*"), []));
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData("/Reports/Finance")]
    [InlineData("/reports/finance/")]
    [InlineData("  /reports/finance  ")]
    public void EvaluatePath_normalises_the_path(string path)
    {
        var decision = PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluatePath(Subjects.Active("reports.view", "reports.finance"), PageTree.Standard().Pages, path);

        Assert.NotNull(decision);
        Assert.Equal("/reports/finance", decision.Page.Path);
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData("/does-not-exist")]
    [InlineData("reports")]    // not a path
    [InlineData("")]
    [InlineData("/a//b")]
    public void EvaluatePath_returns_null_for_unknown_or_invalid_paths(string path)
    {
        Assert.Null(PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluatePath(Subjects.Active("*"), PageTree.Standard().Pages, path));
    }
}

Two of these tests were wrong the first time they were written, and the evaluator was right. The first draft of Wildcard_grant_does_not_cover_the_parent_permission_itself used the standard tree, where /reports requires reports.view, and asserted that reports.* would be refused there. But reports.* does cover reports.view. The failing test was a misunderstanding of my own rule, caught in seconds because the rule was written down and the test was precise. The comment in the test records it. This happens in timed tests too: when a test you wrote fails, re-read the requirement before you touch the code.

7.5 The same problem in 40 minutes

In the test you will not have Result, Permission or a page tree class. You will have whatever input types the scenario gives you. The shape of the answer transfers directly:

  1. A comment with the requirements and your edge-case decisions.
  2. Index the input once (Dictionary<string, Page> by normalised path).
  3. One small function per rule (ParentAllows, RolesAllow).
  4. Memoise per user, guard against cycles with a visiting set.
  5. A test per decision.

Kata 1 (katas/PageAccessKata, Chapter 25) is exactly that, with a model answer of about a hundred lines. Do it against the clock at least twice.

Chapter 8 · Sign-ins and the Compromise Detector

The skill test’s third scenario is an Angular one: show a user when their account may be compromised. Showing is only honest if the verdict is right, so Sentinel computes it on the server, in the domain, where it can be tested exhaustively. This chapter builds that verdict. Chapters 17 and 18 show it.

8.1 Where a sign-in came from

src/Sentinel.Domain/Security/GeoLocation.cs 
namespace Sentinel.Domain.Security;

/// <summary>
/// Where a sign-in appeared to come from, as resolved from its IP address.
/// IP geolocation is approximate: city-level at best, and wrong for VPNs.
/// Treat it as evidence, never as proof.
/// </summary>
public sealed record GeoLocation
{
    public const string UnknownCountryCode = "ZZ"; // ISO 3166 user-assigned "unknown"
    private const double EarthRadiusKm = 6371.0;

    private GeoLocation(string countryCode, string city, double? latitude, double? longitude)
    {
        CountryCode = countryCode;
        City = city;
        Latitude = latitude;
        Longitude = longitude;
    }

    public string CountryCode { get; }
    public string City { get; }
    public double? Latitude { get; }
    public double? Longitude { get; }

    public bool IsKnown => CountryCode != UnknownCountryCode;
    public bool HasCoordinates => Latitude.HasValue && Longitude.HasValue;

    public static GeoLocation Unknown { get; } = new(UnknownCountryCode, "Unknown", null, null);

    public static GeoLocation Create(string countryCode, string city, double latitude, double longitude)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(countryCode) || countryCode.Trim().Length != 2)
            throw new ArgumentException("Country code must be ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.", nameof(countryCode));
        if (latitude is < -90 or > 90)
            throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(latitude));
        if (longitude is < -180 or > 180)
            throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(longitude));

        return new GeoLocation(countryCode.Trim().ToUpperInvariant(), city.Trim(), latitude, longitude);
    }

    /// <summary>Rehydrates a stored location. Null coordinates mean "unknown".</summary>
    public static GeoLocation Restore(string countryCode, string city, double? latitude, double? longitude) =>
        countryCode == UnknownCountryCode || latitude is null || longitude is null
            ? Unknown
            : Create(countryCode, city, latitude.Value, longitude.Value);

    /// <summary>
    /// Great-circle distance by the haversine formula, or null when either
    /// end has no coordinates. Accurate to about 0.5%, which is far better
    /// than the IP lookup that produced the coordinates.
    /// </summary>
    public double? DistanceKmTo(GeoLocation other)
    {
        if (!HasCoordinates || !other.HasCoordinates)
            return null;

        var lat1 = ToRadians(Latitude!.Value);
        var lat2 = ToRadians(other.Latitude!.Value);
        var dLat = lat2 - lat1;
        var dLon = ToRadians(other.Longitude!.Value - Longitude!.Value);

        var a = Math.Pow(Math.Sin(dLat / 2), 2) +
                Math.Cos(lat1) * Math.Cos(lat2) * Math.Pow(Math.Sin(dLon / 2), 2);

        return 2 * EarthRadiusKm * Math.Asin(Math.Sqrt(a));
    }

    public override string ToString() => IsKnown ? $"{City}, {CountryCode}" : "Unknown location";

    private static double ToRadians(double degrees) => degrees * Math.PI / 180.0;
}

Three decisions are encoded here:

  • Unknown is a value, not null. GeoLocation.Unknown (country ZZ, the ISO “user-assigned” code) can be passed around, displayed and compared without null checks, and it has no coordinates, so distance calculations involving it return null instead of measuring from the Gulf of Guinea at latitude 0, longitude 0.
  • Distance is the haversine formula. Accurate to about half a percent, which is far better than IP geolocation itself.
  • The summary comment says what the data is worth: evidence, never proof. A VPN puts a Lagos user in Amsterdam.

The device is identified by hashing the user agent:

src/Sentinel.Domain/Security/DeviceFingerprint.cs 
using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Text;

namespace Sentinel.Domain.Security;

/// <summary>
/// A short, stable identifier for "the same browser on the same machine".
/// Real products combine many signals; we hash the user agent, which is
/// enough to demonstrate the rule and honest about being weak evidence.
/// </summary>
public static class DeviceFingerprint
{
    public static string FromUserAgent(string? userAgent)
    {
        var normalised = (userAgent ?? string.Empty).Trim().ToLowerInvariant();
        var hash = SHA256.HashData(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(normalised));
        return Convert.ToHexStringLower(hash)[..16];
    }

    /// <summary>Just enough of a user agent to be recognisable in a sentence.</summary>
    public static string Describe(string userAgent)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(userAgent))
            return "unknown browser";

        string[] known = ["Edg", "Chrome", "Firefox", "Safari", "curl", "python-requests"];
        var browser = known.FirstOrDefault(k => userAgent.Contains(k, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
        var os = userAgent.Contains("Windows", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ? "Windows"
               : userAgent.Contains("Android", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ? "Android"
               : userAgent.Contains("iPhone", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ? "iPhone"
               : userAgent.Contains("Mac OS", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ? "macOS"
               : userAgent.Contains("Linux", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ? "Linux"
               : null;

        return (browser == "Edg" ? "Edge" : browser, os) switch
        {
            (null, null) => "unrecognised client",
            (null, { } o) => o,
            ({ } b, null) => b,
            ({ } b, { } o) => $"{b} on {o}"
        };
    }
}

8.2 The sign-in attempt

src/Sentinel.Domain/Security/SignInAttempt.cs 
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Domain.Security;

public enum SignInFailureReason
{
    WrongPassword,
    WrongSecondFactor,
    AccountLocked,
    AccountSuspended
}

/// <summary>
/// One attempt to sign in, successful or not. Attempts are immutable facts:
/// once recorded they are never edited, only read.
/// </summary>
public sealed class SignInAttempt : AggregateRoot
{
    public const int MaxUserAgentLength = 512;

    private SignInAttempt(
        Guid id, Guid userId, DateTime occurredAtUtc, string ipAddress, GeoLocation location,
        string userAgent, bool succeeded, SignInFailureReason? failureReason) : base(id)
    {
        UserId = userId;
        OccurredAtUtc = occurredAtUtc;
        IpAddress = ipAddress;
        CountryCode = location.CountryCode;
        City = location.City;
        Latitude = location.Latitude;
        Longitude = location.Longitude;
        UserAgent = userAgent;
        DeviceId = DeviceFingerprint.FromUserAgent(userAgent);
        Succeeded = succeeded;
        FailureReason = failureReason;
    }

    // For EF Core.
    private SignInAttempt() { }

    public Guid UserId { get; private set; }

    /// <summary>
    /// Always <see cref="DateTimeKind.Utc"/>. Infrastructure owns the promise
    /// that this survives a round trip through the database; see
    /// <c>UtcDateTimeConverter</c> and Chapter 22 for what happens when it does not.
    /// </summary>
    public DateTime OccurredAtUtc { get; private set; }

    public string IpAddress { get; private set; } = null!;

    // Stored flat so that EF Core maps four plain columns. The value object
    // is rebuilt on read; it has no identity, so nothing is lost.
    public string CountryCode { get; private set; } = null!;
    public string City { get; private set; } = null!;
    public double? Latitude { get; private set; }
    public double? Longitude { get; private set; }

    public GeoLocation Location => GeoLocation.Restore(CountryCode, City, Latitude, Longitude);

    public string UserAgent { get; private set; } = null!;
    public string DeviceId { get; private set; } = null!;
    public bool Succeeded { get; private set; }
    public SignInFailureReason? FailureReason { get; private set; }

    public static Result<SignInAttempt> Record(
        Guid userId,
        DateTime occurredAtUtc,
        string ipAddress,
        GeoLocation location,
        string? userAgent,
        bool succeeded,
        SignInFailureReason? failureReason = null,
        Guid? id = null)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(location);

        if (occurredAtUtc.Kind != DateTimeKind.Utc)
            return SignInAttemptErrors.TimestampNotUtc;

        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(ipAddress) || !System.Net.IPAddress.TryParse(ipAddress.Trim(), out _))
            return SignInAttemptErrors.InvalidIpAddress(ipAddress);

        if (succeeded && failureReason is not null)
            return SignInAttemptErrors.SuccessWithFailureReason;

        if (!succeeded && failureReason is null)
            return SignInAttemptErrors.FailureWithoutReason;

        var agent = (userAgent ?? string.Empty).Trim();
        if (agent.Length > MaxUserAgentLength)
            agent = agent[..MaxUserAgentLength];

        return new SignInAttempt(
            id ?? Guid.CreateVersion7(), userId, occurredAtUtc, ipAddress.Trim(), location,
            agent, succeeded, failureReason);
    }
}

public static class SignInAttemptErrors
{
    public static readonly Error TimestampNotUtc =
        Error.Validation("SignIn.TimestampNotUtc", "Sign-in timestamps must be UTC (end the value with 'Z' or an offset).");

    public static Error InvalidIpAddress(string? ip) =>
        Error.Validation("SignIn.InvalidIpAddress", $"'{ip}' is not a valid IP address.");

    public static readonly Error SuccessWithFailureReason =
        Error.Validation("SignIn.SuccessWithFailureReason", "A successful sign-in cannot have a failure reason.");

    public static readonly Error FailureWithoutReason =
        Error.Validation("SignIn.FailureWithoutReason", "A failed sign-in must say why it failed.");
}

An attempt is an immutable fact: there are no methods that change it. Its invariants are checked once, in Record: the timestamp is UTC, the IP parses, and a success has no failure reason while a failure must have one. The location is stored as four flat columns (Chapter 11 explains why) and rebuilt as a value object on read.

8.3 Findings, severity and the assessment

src/Sentinel.Domain/Security/SecurityFinding.cs 
namespace Sentinel.Domain.Security;

public enum FindingKind
{
    BruteForce,
    ImpossibleTravel,
    NewCountry,
    NewDevice
}

/// <summary>Ordered: a higher value is more serious, so <c>Max()</c> is meaningful.</summary>
public enum Severity
{
    None = 0,
    Low = 1,
    Medium = 2,
    High = 3
}

/// <summary>
/// One reason to think the account may be compromised.
/// </summary>
/// <param name="Key">
/// Stable across recomputation (it is built from attempt ids, not from a
/// counter), so the user can acknowledge it and the acknowledgement sticks.
/// </param>
/// <param name="OccurredAtUtc">When the suspicious attempt happened (the latest one, for a burst).</param>
/// <param name="AttemptIds">The sign-in attempts that are the evidence for this finding.</param>
public sealed record SecurityFinding(
    string Key,
    FindingKind Kind,
    Severity Severity,
    DateTime OccurredAtUtc,
    IReadOnlyList<Guid> AttemptIds,
    string Summary);

/// <summary>The verdict for an account: the findings, and the worst of them.</summary>
public sealed record SecurityAssessment(Severity RiskLevel, IReadOnlyList<SecurityFinding> Findings)
{
    public static SecurityAssessment Clear { get; } = new(Severity.None, []);

    /// <summary>Medium or above: worth interrupting the user about.</summary>
    public bool IsCompromiseSuspected => RiskLevel >= Severity.Medium;
}

Severity has explicit numeric values so that Max() means “worst”. A finding’s Key is built from the id of the attempt that triggered it, so recomputing the assessment tomorrow produces the same key, and the user’s “that was me” sticks.

src/Sentinel.Domain/Security/DetectionPolicy.cs 
namespace Sentinel.Domain.Security;

/// <summary>
/// The thresholds the detector uses. They are data, not constants buried in
/// the rules, because the first thing a security team asks after launch is
/// "can we make it less noisy?", and the answer should be a config change.
/// </summary>
/// <param name="ReportingWindow">Only attempts newer than this produce findings.</param>
/// <param name="FailedAttemptThreshold">Failures within <paramref name="FailedAttemptWindow"/> that count as a brute-force burst.</param>
/// <param name="FailedAttemptWindow">The sliding window for counting failures.</param>
/// <param name="MaxPlausibleSpeedKmh">Faster than this between two sign-ins is "impossible travel". Airliners cruise near 900 km/h.</param>
/// <param name="MinTravelDistanceKm">Ignore jumps shorter than this; IP geolocation is too coarse to judge them.</param>
public sealed record DetectionPolicy(
    TimeSpan ReportingWindow,
    int FailedAttemptThreshold,
    TimeSpan FailedAttemptWindow,
    double MaxPlausibleSpeedKmh,
    double MinTravelDistanceKm)
{
    public static DetectionPolicy Default { get; } = new(
        ReportingWindow: TimeSpan.FromDays(30),
        FailedAttemptThreshold: 5,
        FailedAttemptWindow: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15),
        MaxPlausibleSpeedKmh: 900,
        MinTravelDistanceKm: 500);
}

Thresholds are data. The security team’s first question after launch will be “can it be less noisy?”, and the answer should be a configuration change, not a code review.

8.4 The detector

src/Sentinel.Domain/Security/CompromiseDetector.cs 
namespace Sentinel.Domain.Security;

/// <summary>
/// Looks at one user's sign-in history and says whether the account may be
/// compromised. Four rules, each independent:
/// <list type="bullet">
///   <item><b>Brute force</b>: at least N failures inside a short window. High if a success follows the burst.</item>
///   <item><b>Impossible travel</b>: two successful sign-ins further apart than anyone could travel in the time between them. High.</item>
///   <item><b>New country</b>: a successful sign-in from a country this user has never signed in from. Medium.</item>
///   <item><b>New device</b>: a successful sign-in from a device this user has never used. Low.</item>
/// </list>
/// </summary>
/// <remarks>
/// <para>
/// The history passed in is both the evidence and the baseline. Attempts older
/// than the reporting window never produce findings, but they still count as
/// "seen before" for the new-country and new-device rules. Callers should
/// therefore pass more history than the reporting window: the application
/// layer passes ninety days against a thirty-day window.
/// </para>
/// <para>
/// The detector sorts its input itself and does not trust the caller's order.
/// It cannot, however, notice that the caller sent the wrong <i>subset</i> of
/// history; Chapter 23 is about exactly that.
/// </para>
/// </remarks>
public static class CompromiseDetector
{
    public static SecurityAssessment Assess(
        IEnumerable<SignInAttempt> history,
        DateTime nowUtc,
        IReadOnlySet<string>? acknowledgedKeys = null,
        DetectionPolicy? policy = null)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(history);
        if (nowUtc.Kind != DateTimeKind.Utc)
            throw new ArgumentException("nowUtc must be UTC.", nameof(nowUtc));

        policy ??= DetectionPolicy.Default;
        acknowledgedKeys ??= new HashSet<string>();

        // Oldest first; ties broken by id so the output is deterministic.
        // Attempts "from the future" (clock skew upstream) are ignored rather
        // than allowed to poison the baseline.
        var ordered = history
            .Where(a => a.OccurredAtUtc <= nowUtc)
            .OrderBy(a => a.OccurredAtUtc)
            .ThenBy(a => a.Id)
            .ToList();

        if (ordered.Count == 0)
            return SecurityAssessment.Clear;

        var reportFrom = nowUtc - policy.ReportingWindow;

        var findings = DetectBruteForce(ordered, policy)
            .Concat(DetectImpossibleTravel(ordered, policy))
            .Concat(DetectNewCountries(ordered))
            .Concat(DetectNewDevices(ordered))
            .Where(f => f.OccurredAtUtc >= reportFrom)
            .Where(f => !acknowledgedKeys.Contains(f.Key))
            .OrderByDescending(f => f.Severity)
            .ThenByDescending(f => f.OccurredAtUtc)
            .ToList();

        var riskLevel = findings.Count == 0 ? Severity.None : findings.Max(f => f.Severity);
        return new SecurityAssessment(riskLevel, findings);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Groups failures into bursts (a gap longer than the window ends a burst),
    /// then reports a burst when some window-sized slice of it holds at least
    /// the threshold number of failures.
    /// </summary>
    private static IEnumerable<SecurityFinding> DetectBruteForce(List<SignInAttempt> ordered, DetectionPolicy policy)
    {
        var failures = ordered.Where(a => !a.Succeeded).ToList();
        var burst = new List<SignInAttempt>();

        foreach (var failure in failures)
        {
            if (burst.Count > 0 && failure.OccurredAtUtc - burst[^1].OccurredAtUtc > policy.FailedAttemptWindow)
            {
                if (TryReportBurst(burst, ordered, policy) is { } finding)
                    yield return finding;
                burst = [];
            }

            burst.Add(failure);
        }

        if (TryReportBurst(burst, ordered, policy) is { } last)
            yield return last;
    }

    private static SecurityFinding? TryReportBurst(List<SignInAttempt> burst, List<SignInAttempt> ordered, DetectionPolicy policy)
    {
        if (burst.Count < policy.FailedAttemptThreshold || MaxInAnyWindow(burst, policy.FailedAttemptWindow) < policy.FailedAttemptThreshold)
            return null;

        var first = burst[0];
        var last = burst[^1];

        // Did the attacker get in? A success shortly after the burst is the
        // difference between "someone is trying" and "someone succeeded".
        var successAfter = ordered.FirstOrDefault(a =>
            a.Succeeded &&
            a.OccurredAtUtc > first.OccurredAtUtc &&
            a.OccurredAtUtc <= last.OccurredAtUtc + policy.FailedAttemptWindow);

        var evidence = burst.Select(a => a.Id).ToList();
        if (successAfter is not null)
            evidence.Add(successAfter.Id);

        var countries = burst.Select(a => a.Location).Where(l => l.IsKnown).Select(l => l.CountryCode).Distinct().ToList();
        var from = countries.Count == 0 ? "an unknown location" : string.Join(", ", countries);

        return new SecurityFinding(
            Key: $"brute-force:{first.Id:N}",
            Kind: FindingKind.BruteForce,
            Severity: successAfter is null ? Severity.Medium : Severity.High,
            OccurredAtUtc: successAfter?.OccurredAtUtc ?? last.OccurredAtUtc,
            AttemptIds: evidence,
            Summary: successAfter is null
                ? $"{burst.Count} failed sign-in attempts from {from} in a short period."
                : $"{burst.Count} failed sign-in attempts from {from}, followed by a successful sign-in.");
    }

    /// <summary>Two-pointer sweep: the most failures that fit inside any one window.</summary>
    private static int MaxInAnyWindow(List<SignInAttempt> burst, TimeSpan window)
    {
        var best = 0;
        var start = 0;
        for (var end = 0; end < burst.Count; end++)
        {
            while (burst[end].OccurredAtUtc - burst[start].OccurredAtUtc > window)
                start++;
            best = Math.Max(best, end - start + 1);
        }
        return best;
    }

    private static IEnumerable<SecurityFinding> DetectImpossibleTravel(List<SignInAttempt> ordered, DetectionPolicy policy)
    {
        SignInAttempt? previous = null;

        foreach (var current in ordered.Where(a => a.Succeeded && a.Location.HasCoordinates))
        {
            if (previous is not null && previous.Location.DistanceKmTo(current.Location) is { } km && km >= policy.MinTravelDistanceKm)
            {
                var hours = (current.OccurredAtUtc - previous.OccurredAtUtc).TotalHours;

                // Zero elapsed time over 500 km is the clearest case of all;
                // guard the division rather than letting it produce infinity.
                var speedKmh = hours <= 0 ? double.PositiveInfinity : km / hours;

                if (speedKmh > policy.MaxPlausibleSpeedKmh)
                {
                    yield return new SecurityFinding(
                        Key: $"impossible-travel:{current.Id:N}",
                        Kind: FindingKind.ImpossibleTravel,
                        Severity: Severity.High,
                        OccurredAtUtc: current.OccurredAtUtc,
                        AttemptIds: [previous.Id, current.Id],
                        Summary: $"Signed in from {previous.Location} and then {current.Location} " +
                                 $"{FormatElapsed(current.OccurredAtUtc - previous.OccurredAtUtc)} later ({km:N0} km apart).");
                }
            }

            previous = current;
        }
    }

    private static IEnumerable<SecurityFinding> DetectNewCountries(List<SignInAttempt> ordered)
    {
        var seen = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
        var isFirstSuccess = true;

        foreach (var attempt in ordered.Where(a => a.Succeeded && a.Location.IsKnown))
        {
            // The very first success sets the baseline. Without history there
            // is nothing to compare against, and flagging every new account
            // as "new country" would train users to ignore the banner.
            if (seen.Add(attempt.Location.CountryCode) && !isFirstSuccess)
            {
                yield return new SecurityFinding(
                    Key: $"new-country:{attempt.Id:N}",
                    Kind: FindingKind.NewCountry,
                    Severity: Severity.Medium,
                    OccurredAtUtc: attempt.OccurredAtUtc,
                    AttemptIds: [attempt.Id],
                    Summary: $"First sign-in from {attempt.Location}.");
            }

            isFirstSuccess = false;
        }
    }

    private static IEnumerable<SecurityFinding> DetectNewDevices(List<SignInAttempt> ordered)
    {
        var seen = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
        var isFirstSuccess = true;

        foreach (var attempt in ordered.Where(a => a.Succeeded))
        {
            if (seen.Add(attempt.DeviceId) && !isFirstSuccess)
            {
                yield return new SecurityFinding(
                    Key: $"new-device:{attempt.Id:N}",
                    Kind: FindingKind.NewDevice,
                    Severity: Severity.Low,
                    OccurredAtUtc: attempt.OccurredAtUtc,
                    AttemptIds: [attempt.Id],
                    Summary: $"Sign-in from a device not seen before ({DeviceFingerprint.Describe(attempt.UserAgent)}).");
            }

            isFirstSuccess = false;
        }
    }

    private static string FormatElapsed(TimeSpan elapsed) => elapsed.TotalMinutes < 60
        ? $"{Math.Max(0, (int)elapsed.TotalMinutes)} minutes"
        : $"{elapsed.TotalHours:0.#} hours";
}

The brute-force rule, carefully

“At least five failures within fifteen minutes” sounds simple and hides two traps.

Trap one: what counts as “within”? Five failures ten minutes apart are within forty minutes of each other but never more than two inside any fifteen-minute window. The detector first groups failures into bursts (a gap longer than the window ends a burst), then uses a two-pointer sweep, MaxInAnyWindow, to find the most failures inside any window-sized slice. Failures_spread_more_thinly_than_the_window_allows_are_not_a_burst pins that behaviour.

Trap two: did the attacker get in? Failures alone mean someone is trying. A success shortly after them means someone may have succeeded. The detector looks for a success after the first failure and within a window of the last, raises the severity to High, and adds the success to the evidence, so the table highlights it.

The impossible-travel rule

Only successful attempts with coordinates are compared, each with the one before it. Two guards matter:

  • Short hops are ignored (below 500 km). IP geolocation cannot tell Lagos from Ikeja, so “travelling” 9 km in a minute is noise.
  • Zero elapsed time is the clearest case, not a division by zero. The speed is set to infinity explicitly, rather than letting km / 0.0 produce it by accident.

New country and new device

Both walk successes in order with a HashSet of what has been seen. The first success sets the baseline and is never reported: flagging every new account would teach users to ignore the banner, and a security warning that is ignored is worse than none.

What the detector refuses to trust

It sorts its input itself (oldest first, ties by id, so the output is deterministic), ignores attempts dated after now, and requires now to be UTC. What it cannot do is notice that it has been handed the wrong subset of history. Remember that sentence; Chapter 23 is about it.

8.5 The tests

tests/Sentinel.Domain.Tests/Security/CompromiseDetectorTests.cs 
using Sentinel.Domain.Security;

namespace Sentinel.Domain.Tests.Security;

public class CompromiseDetectorTests
{
    private static readonly DateTime Now = History.Now;

    private static SecurityAssessment Assess(History history, IReadOnlySet<string>? acknowledged = null) =>
        CompromiseDetector.Assess(history.Attempts, Now, acknowledged);

    // ---- Nothing to see ----

    [Fact]
    public void No_history_is_clear()
    {
        var assessment = CompromiseDetector.Assess([], Now);

        Assert.Equal(Severity.None, assessment.RiskLevel);
        Assert.Empty(assessment.Findings);
        Assert.False(assessment.IsCompromiseSuspected);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void An_ordinary_history_is_clear()
    {
        var assessment = Assess(new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline().Success(Now.AddHours(-1)));

        Assert.Equal(Severity.None, assessment.RiskLevel);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void The_first_ever_sign_in_is_not_new_anything()
    {
        // No baseline yet: flagging it would flag every new account.
        var assessment = Assess(new History().Success(Now.AddHours(-1), Places.London, Agents.Phone));

        Assert.Empty(assessment.Findings);
    }

    // ---- Brute force ----

    [Fact]
    public void Failures_below_the_threshold_are_not_a_burst()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Failures(Now.AddHours(-2), count: 4, spacing: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1));

        Assert.DoesNotContain(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.BruteForce);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Threshold_failures_inside_the_window_are_a_medium_finding()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Failures(Now.AddHours(-2), count: 5, spacing: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2), where: Places.Frankfurt);

        var finding = Assert.Single(Assess(history).Findings);

        Assert.Equal(FindingKind.BruteForce, finding.Kind);
        Assert.Equal(Severity.Medium, finding.Severity);
        Assert.Equal(5, finding.AttemptIds.Count);
        Assert.Contains("DE", finding.Summary);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Failures_spread_more_thinly_than_the_window_allows_are_not_a_burst()
    {
        // Ten minutes apart: never more than two inside any fifteen minutes.
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Failures(Now.AddHours(-3), count: 8, spacing: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10));

        Assert.DoesNotContain(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.BruteForce);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void A_success_straight_after_the_burst_makes_it_high_and_cites_the_success()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Failures(Now.AddHours(-2), count: 6, spacing: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30))
            .Success(Now.AddHours(-2).AddMinutes(4));

        var finding = Assert.Single(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.BruteForce);

        Assert.Equal(Severity.High, finding.Severity);
        Assert.Contains(history.Last.Id, finding.AttemptIds);
        Assert.Equal(history.Last.OccurredAtUtc, finding.OccurredAtUtc);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Two_separate_bursts_are_two_findings()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Failures(Now.AddDays(-3), count: 5, spacing: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1))
            .Failures(Now.AddDays(-1), count: 5, spacing: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1));

        Assert.Equal(2, Assess(history).Findings.Count(f => f.Kind == FindingKind.BruteForce));
    }

    // ---- Impossible travel ----

    [Fact]
    public void Lagos_then_London_forty_minutes_later_is_impossible_travel()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Success(Now.AddHours(-5), Places.Lagos)
            .Success(Now.AddHours(-5).AddMinutes(40), Places.London);

        var finding = Assert.Single(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.ImpossibleTravel);

        Assert.Equal(Severity.High, finding.Severity);
        Assert.Equal(2, finding.AttemptIds.Count);
        Assert.Contains("40 minutes", finding.Summary);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void New_York_then_London_a_day_later_is_plausible()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-2), Places.NewYork)
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-1), Places.London);

        Assert.DoesNotContain(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.ImpossibleTravel);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Short_hops_are_ignored_because_ip_geolocation_is_too_coarse()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Success(Now.AddHours(-1), Places.Lagos)
            .Success(Now.AddHours(-1).AddMinutes(1), Places.Ikeja);

        Assert.DoesNotContain(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.ImpossibleTravel);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Simultaneous_sign_ins_far_apart_do_not_divide_by_zero()
    {
        var at = Now.AddHours(-1);
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Success(at, Places.Lagos)
            .Success(at, Places.London);

        Assert.Contains(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.ImpossibleTravel);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Unknown_locations_are_skipped_rather_than_treated_as_zero_zero()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Success(Now.AddHours(-2), GeoLocation.Unknown)
            .Success(Now.AddHours(-1), Places.Lagos);

        Assert.DoesNotContain(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.ImpossibleTravel);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Failed_attempts_do_not_count_as_travel()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Success(Now.AddHours(-2), Places.Lagos)
            .Failure(Now.AddHours(-2).AddMinutes(5), Places.London);

        Assert.DoesNotContain(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.ImpossibleTravel);
    }

    // ---- New country, new device ----

    [Fact]
    public void A_success_from_a_new_country_is_medium()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline().Success(Now.AddDays(-1), Places.London);

        var finding = Assert.Single(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.NewCountry);

        Assert.Equal(Severity.Medium, finding.Severity);
        Assert.Contains("London, GB", finding.Summary);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Only_the_first_sign_in_from_a_country_is_new()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-3), Places.London)
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-2), Places.London);

        Assert.Single(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.NewCountry);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void A_failure_from_a_new_country_neither_raises_nor_establishes_it()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Failure(Now.AddDays(-2), Places.Frankfurt)
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-1), Places.Frankfurt);

        // The later success is still the first *successful* sign-in from DE.
        var finding = Assert.Single(Assess(history).Findings, f => f.Kind == FindingKind.NewCountry);
        Assert.Equal(history.Last.Id, Assert.Single(finding.AttemptIds));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void A_new_device_is_low()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline().Success(Now.AddDays(-1), agent: Agents.Phone);

        var finding = Assert.Single(Assess(history).Findings);

        Assert.Equal(FindingKind.NewDevice, finding.Kind);
        Assert.Equal(Severity.Low, finding.Severity);
        Assert.Contains("Safari on iPhone", finding.Summary);
        Assert.False(Assess(history).IsCompromiseSuspected);
    }

    // ---- Windows, acknowledgements, robustness ----

    [Fact]
    public void Findings_older_than_the_reporting_window_are_not_reported_but_still_count_as_baseline()
    {
        var history = new History()
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-80), Places.Lagos)
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-60), Places.London)  // new country, but 60 days ago
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-1), Places.London);   // London is no longer new

        Assert.Empty(Assess(history).Findings);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Acknowledged_findings_are_excluded_and_the_risk_level_drops()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-1), Places.London, Agents.Phone);
        var before = Assess(history);
        var newCountry = before.Findings.Single(f => f.Kind == FindingKind.NewCountry);

        var after = Assess(history, new HashSet<string> { newCountry.Key });

        Assert.Equal(Severity.Medium, before.RiskLevel);
        Assert.Equal(Severity.Low, after.RiskLevel);
        Assert.DoesNotContain(after.Findings, f => f.Key == newCountry.Key);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Finding_keys_are_stable_across_assessments()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline().Success(Now.AddDays(-1), Places.London);

        Assert.Equal(
            Assess(history).Findings.Select(f => f.Key),
            Assess(history).Findings.Select(f => f.Key));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Input_order_does_not_matter()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Success(Now.AddHours(-5), Places.Lagos)
            .Success(Now.AddHours(-5).AddMinutes(40), Places.London);

        var shuffled = history.Attempts.OrderBy(_ => Guid.NewGuid()).ToList();

        Assert.Equal(
            Assess(history).Findings.Select(f => f.Key),
            CompromiseDetector.Assess(shuffled, Now).Findings.Select(f => f.Key));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Attempts_after_now_are_ignored()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline().Success(Now.AddHours(1), Places.London);

        Assert.Empty(Assess(history).Findings);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Findings_are_ordered_most_severe_first_then_newest_first()
    {
        var history = new History().WithOrdinaryBaseline()
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-3), agent: Agents.Phone)            // low
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-2), Places.Lagos)
            .Success(Now.AddDays(-2).AddMinutes(30), Places.London);  // high + medium

        var severities = Assess(history).Findings.Select(f => f.Severity).ToList();

        Assert.Equal(severities.OrderByDescending(s => s), severities);
        Assert.Equal(Severity.High, severities[0]);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Now_must_be_utc()
    {
        Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => CompromiseDetector.Assess([], DateTime.Now));
    }
}

These tests are organised by rule, and each rule has tests for both sides of its boundary: four failures and five, ten minutes apart and two, 9 km and 5,000 km. That habit (test just inside and just outside every threshold) is the single most reliable way to “handle edge cases” in a timed test.

8.6 Doing it in the browser instead

In the test, you may be given raw login events in Angular and asked to decide what looks suspicious there. The same rules translate directly to TypeScript: sort a copy ([...events].sort(...), never sort the input in place), walk it once, keep Sets of seen countries and devices, and return findings rather than booleans so the template can explain itself. Chapter 17 shows where such a function belongs in a component tree (a pure function in its own file, called by the container) and Chapter 20 how to test it.

Chapter 9 · The Application Layer

The Application layer turns requests into calls on the domain. Its machinery (messages, handlers, a dispatcher, a pipeline) is small, and writing it yourself is the fastest way to understand what MediatR and its relatives do.

9.1 The messages

src/Sentinel.Application/Abstractions/Messaging/Requests.cs 
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;

/// <summary>
/// Anything the dispatcher can send. Every response is a <see cref="Result"/>,
/// so a caller always has to look at the outcome before it can use a value.
/// </summary>
public interface IRequest<TResponse> where TResponse : Result;

/// <summary>Changes state and returns nothing but success or failure.</summary>
public interface ICommand : IRequest<Result>;

/// <summary>Changes state and returns a value, typically the id of something created.</summary>
public interface ICommand<TValue> : IRequest<Result<TValue>>;

/// <summary>Reads state. A query must never change anything.</summary>
public interface IQuery<TValue> : IRequest<Result<TValue>>;

Every request declares its response type, and every response is a Result. The compiler therefore knows that dispatcher.Send(new GetUserByIdQuery(id)) returns Result<UserDetailDto>; no casts anywhere.

src/Sentinel.Application/Abstractions/Messaging/Handlers.cs 
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;

/// <summary>
/// The one interface the dispatcher knows about. The three below exist so a
/// handler's declaration says what kind of request it serves.
/// </summary>
public interface IRequestHandler<in TRequest, TResponse>
    where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
    where TResponse : Result
{
    Task<TResponse> Handle(TRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}

public interface ICommandHandler<in TCommand> : IRequestHandler<TCommand, Result>
    where TCommand : ICommand;

public interface ICommandHandler<in TCommand, TValue> : IRequestHandler<TCommand, Result<TValue>>
    where TCommand : ICommand<TValue>;

public interface IQueryHandler<in TQuery, TValue> : IRequestHandler<TQuery, Result<TValue>>
    where TQuery : IQuery<TValue>;

The dispatcher only knows IRequestHandler<TRequest, TResponse>. The three specialised interfaces exist for the reader: a class that implements IQueryHandler<,> tells you at a glance that it must not change state.

9.2 The pipeline

src/Sentinel.Application/Abstractions/Messaging/IPipelineBehavior.cs 
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;

/// <summary>Calls the next behaviour in the pipeline, or the handler itself at the end.</summary>
public delegate Task<TResponse> RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse>();

/// <summary>
/// Code that wraps every handler: validation, logging, timing. Behaviours are
/// the Decorator pattern applied by the dispatcher, which is how cross-cutting
/// concerns stay out of the handlers (the S and O of SOLID in one interface).
/// </summary>
public interface IPipelineBehavior<in TRequest, TResponse>
    where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
    where TResponse : Result
{
    Task<TResponse> Handle(TRequest request, RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse> next, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}

A behaviour receives the request and a delegate for “the rest of the pipeline”. It can act before, after, or instead of calling it. That is the Decorator pattern, applied uniformly to every handler.

9.3 The dispatcher

src/Sentinel.Application/Abstractions/Messaging/Dispatcher.cs 
using System.Collections.Concurrent;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;

/// <summary>Sends a request to its single handler, through the pipeline.</summary>
public interface IDispatcher
{
    Task<TResponse> Send<TResponse>(IRequest<TResponse> request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        where TResponse : Result;
}

/// <summary>
/// Our replacement for MediatR's <c>ISender</c>. The only clever part is the
/// wrapper: <see cref="Send{TResponse}"/> knows the response type statically
/// but the request type only at run time, and DI needs both to resolve
/// <c>IRequestHandler&lt;TRequest, TResponse&gt;</c>. A closed generic wrapper,
/// built once per request type with reflection and cached, bridges the gap so
/// that every call after the first is ordinary, strongly-typed code.
/// </summary>
public sealed class Dispatcher(IServiceProvider services) : IDispatcher
{
    private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Type, object> Wrappers = new();

    public Task<TResponse> Send<TResponse>(IRequest<TResponse> request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        where TResponse : Result
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(request);

        var wrapper = (RequestHandlerWrapper<TResponse>)Wrappers.GetOrAdd(
            request.GetType(),
            requestType => Activator.CreateInstance(
                typeof(RequestHandlerWrapper<,>).MakeGenericType(requestType, typeof(TResponse)))!);

        return wrapper.Handle(request, services, cancellationToken);
    }
}

internal abstract class RequestHandlerWrapper<TResponse> where TResponse : Result
{
    public abstract Task<TResponse> Handle(IRequest<TResponse> request, IServiceProvider services, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}

internal sealed class RequestHandlerWrapper<TRequest, TResponse> : RequestHandlerWrapper<TResponse>
    where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
    where TResponse : Result
{
    public override Task<TResponse> Handle(IRequest<TResponse> request, IServiceProvider services, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var typedRequest = (TRequest)request;
        var handler = services.GetRequiredService<IRequestHandler<TRequest, TResponse>>();

        RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse> pipeline = () => handler.Handle(typedRequest, cancellationToken);

        // Registered first runs outermost: wrap in reverse so that
        // AddBehavior(A); AddBehavior(B) gives A(B(handler)).
        foreach (var behavior in services.GetServices<IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>>().Reverse())
        {
            var next = pipeline;
            pipeline = () => behavior.Handle(typedRequest, next, cancellationToken);
        }

        return pipeline();
    }
}

The interesting problem is generic type resolution. Send<TResponse> knows the response type at compile time, but the concrete request type (GetUserByIdQuery) only at run time, and DI needs both to resolve IRequestHandler<GetUserByIdQuery, Result<UserDetailDto>>. The solution:

  1. On the first Send for a request type, build the closed generic type RequestHandlerWrapper<GetUserByIdQuery, Result<UserDetailDto>> with MakeGenericType and create one instance.
  2. Cache it in a ConcurrentDictionary keyed by request type.
  3. From then on, call it through the abstract base RequestHandlerWrapper<TResponse>, whose Handle is ordinary, strongly-typed code.

Reflection runs once per request type for the life of the process.

Behaviours are wrapped in reverse registration order so that the first one registered runs outermost: register logging then validation, and a rejected request is still logged.

9.4 Validation without a library

src/Sentinel.Application/Abstractions/Validation/Validation.cs 
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Validation;

public sealed record ValidationFailure(string Property, string Message);

/// <summary>
/// An <see cref="Error"/> carrying one message per offending field, which the
/// API turns into an RFC 9457 validation problem response.
/// </summary>
public sealed record ValidationError(IReadOnlyList<ValidationFailure> Failures)
    : Error("Validation.Failed", "One or more fields are invalid.", ErrorType.Validation);

/// <summary>
/// Checks the <i>shape</i> of a request: required fields, lengths, ranges.
/// Rules that need the database ("is this email taken?") belong in the
/// handler; rules about the business belong in the domain.
/// </summary>
public interface IValidator<in TRequest>
{
    IEnumerable<ValidationFailure> Validate(TRequest request);
}

/// <summary>
/// A tiny base class in place of FluentValidation. It is not a framework:
/// it is three helpers that make a validator read like a checklist.
/// </summary>
public abstract class Validator<TRequest> : IValidator<TRequest>
{
    public abstract IEnumerable<ValidationFailure> Validate(TRequest request);

    protected static IEnumerable<ValidationFailure> Required(string? value, string property)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value))
            yield return new ValidationFailure(property, $"{property} is required.");
    }

    protected static IEnumerable<ValidationFailure> MaxLength(string? value, int max, string property)
    {
        if (value is not null && value.Trim().Length > max)
            yield return new ValidationFailure(property, $"{property} cannot exceed {max} characters.");
    }

    protected static IEnumerable<ValidationFailure> InRange(int value, int min, int max, string property)
    {
        if (value < min || value > max)
            yield return new ValidationFailure(property, $"{property} must be between {min} and {max}.");
    }
}

FluentValidation is excellent; it is also a dependency for something that, in this application, needs three helpers. Writing them shows the boundary that matters more than the library:

Kind of rule Example Where it lives
Shape “Email is required”, “PageSize between 1 and 100” Validator
Needs the database “That email is already registered” Handler
Business invariant “A role cannot be granted twice” Domain

A validator that queries the database, or a handler that checks required fields, is a sign the layers have blurred.

9.5 The behaviours

src/Sentinel.Application/Behaviors/ValidationBehavior.cs 
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Validation;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Behaviors;

/// <summary>
/// Runs every validator registered for the request and short-circuits with a
/// <see cref="ValidationError"/> if any of them complain. The handler is
/// never called with a malformed request, so it never has to check.
/// </summary>
internal sealed class ValidationBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>(IEnumerable<IValidator<TRequest>> validators)
    : IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>
    where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
    where TResponse : Result
{
    public Task<TResponse> Handle(TRequest request, RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse> next, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var failures = validators
            .SelectMany(v => v.Validate(request))
            .ToList();

        return failures.Count == 0
            ? next()
            : Task.FromResult(ResultFactory.Failure<TResponse>(new ValidationError(failures)));
    }
}

When validation fails, the behaviour must return a failed TResponse without knowing what TResponse is beyond “some Result”:

src/Sentinel.Application/Behaviors/ResultFactory.cs 
using System.Collections.Concurrent;
using System.Reflection;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Behaviors;

/// <summary>
/// Builds a failed <typeparamref name="TResponse"/> when all a behaviour
/// knows is that TResponse is "some kind of Result". For <c>Result</c> that
/// is a direct call; for <c>Result&lt;T&gt;</c> the T is only known at run
/// time, so the factory method is found by reflection once and cached.
/// </summary>
internal static class ResultFactory
{
    private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Type, Func<Error, Result>> Factories = new();

    public static TResponse Failure<TResponse>(Error error) where TResponse : Result
    {
        if (typeof(TResponse) == typeof(Result))
            return (TResponse)Result.Failure(error);

        var factory = Factories.GetOrAdd(typeof(TResponse), static type =>
        {
            // DeclaredOnly: Result<T>.Failure hides Result.Failure, and we want the one on Result<T>.
            var method = type.GetMethod(
                nameof(Result.Failure),
                BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly,
                [typeof(Error)])
                ?? throw new InvalidOperationException($"{type} has no static Failure(Error) method.");

            return method.CreateDelegate<Func<Error, Result>>();
        });

        return (TResponse)factory(error);
    }
}

BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly matters: Result<T> declares its own static Failure that hides the base one, and we want the one that returns Result<T>.

src/Sentinel.Application/Behaviors/LoggingBehavior.cs 
using System.Diagnostics;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Behaviors;

/// <summary>
/// Logs every request's name, outcome and duration. When a support ticket
/// arrives with nothing but a time and a user, this log line is usually the
/// first evidence you have (Chapter 21).
/// </summary>
internal sealed partial class LoggingBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>(ILogger<LoggingBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>> logger)
    : IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>
    where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
    where TResponse : Result
{
    public async Task<TResponse> Handle(TRequest request, RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse> next, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var requestName = typeof(TRequest).Name;
        var started = Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();

        var response = await next();

        var elapsedMs = Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime(started).TotalMilliseconds;
        if (response.IsSuccess)
            LogSucceeded(requestName, elapsedMs);
        else
            LogFailed(requestName, response.Error!.Code, response.Error.Message, elapsedMs);

        return response;
    }

    [LoggerMessage(Level = LogLevel.Information, Message = "{RequestName} succeeded in {ElapsedMs:0.0} ms")]
    private partial void LogSucceeded(string requestName, double elapsedMs);

    [LoggerMessage(Level = LogLevel.Warning, Message = "{RequestName} failed with {ErrorCode} ({ErrorMessage}) in {ElapsedMs:0.0} ms")]
    private partial void LogFailed(string requestName, string errorCode, string errorMessage, double elapsedMs);
}

[LoggerMessage] generates the logging code at compile time: no boxing, no parsing the template on every call, and structured properties (RequestName, ErrorCode) that you can filter on. When a ticket arrives with nothing but “it failed around 10 this morning”, these lines are your first evidence (Chapter 21).

9.6 The ports

src/Sentinel.Application/Abstractions/Ports/Ports.cs 
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Sentinel.Domain.Pages;
using Sentinel.Domain.Roles;
using Sentinel.Domain.Security;
using Sentinel.Domain.Users;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Ports;

/// <summary>
/// The persistence port. Infrastructure implements it with EF Core; handlers
/// use it with LINQ. There is no repository layer on top (Chapter 3 explains
/// why), and this interface is the reason none is needed: it is owned by
/// Application, so the dependency rule holds.
/// </summary>
public interface IApplicationDbContext
{
    DbSet<User> Users { get; }
    DbSet<Role> Roles { get; }
    DbSet<Page> Pages { get; }
    DbSet<SignInAttempt> SignInAttempts { get; }
    DbSet<FindingAcknowledgement> FindingAcknowledgements { get; }

    Task<int> SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}

/// <summary>
/// The current time, injectable. A handler that calls <c>DateTime.UtcNow</c>
/// directly cannot be tested at "thirty-one days later".
/// </summary>
public interface IClock
{
    DateTime UtcNow { get; }
}

/// <summary>Resolves an IP address to an approximate location.</summary>
public interface IGeoLocator
{
    GeoLocation Locate(string ipAddress);
}

IClock deserves a word. A handler that calls DateTime.UtcNow directly cannot be tested at “thirty-one days later”, and every time-based rule in this system (reporting windows, clock skew, relative times) needs exactly that. Every “now” in Sentinel comes from an IClock, on the server, and from a Clock service in Angular.

9.7 Registering everything

src/Sentinel.Application/DependencyInjection.cs 
using System.Reflection;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Validation;
using Sentinel.Application.Behaviors;
using Sentinel.Application.Security;
using Sentinel.Domain.Security;

namespace Sentinel.Application;

public static class DependencyInjection
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Registers the dispatcher, the pipeline, and every handler and validator
    /// in this assembly. Adding a slice never means editing this file.
    /// </summary>
    public static IServiceCollection AddApplication(this IServiceCollection services, DetectionPolicy? detectionPolicy = null)
    {
        services.AddScoped<IDispatcher, Dispatcher>();

        // Order matters: logging wraps validation, so rejected requests are logged too.
        services.AddScoped(typeof(IPipelineBehavior<,>), typeof(LoggingBehavior<,>));
        services.AddScoped(typeof(IPipelineBehavior<,>), typeof(ValidationBehavior<,>));

        var assembly = Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly();
        RegisterClosedImplementations(services, assembly, typeof(IRequestHandler<,>));
        RegisterClosedImplementations(services, assembly, typeof(IValidator<>));

        services.AddSingleton(detectionPolicy ?? DetectionPolicy.Default);
        services.AddScoped<AccountAssessor>();

        return services;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// For every concrete class implementing a closed form of
    /// <paramref name="openInterface"/>, register it against that closed form.
    /// This is the twenty lines of assembly scanning that Scrutor would
    /// otherwise provide.
    /// </summary>
    private static void RegisterClosedImplementations(IServiceCollection services, Assembly assembly, Type openInterface)
    {
        var registrations =
            from type in assembly.GetTypes()
            where type is { IsClass: true, IsAbstract: false, IsGenericTypeDefinition: false }
            from implemented in type.GetInterfaces()
            where implemented.IsGenericType && implemented.GetGenericTypeDefinition() == openInterface
            select (Service: implemented, Implementation: type);

        foreach (var (service, implementation) in registrations)
            services.AddScoped(service, implementation);
    }
}

Adding a slice never touches this file: the scan finds every closed implementation of IRequestHandler<,> and IValidator<>. That is the open/closed principle doing visible work.

Chapter 10 · Feature Slices

Each use case is a folder with a request (and its validator) in one file and its handler in another. This chapter walks through the slices that matter for the skill test, and lists the rest.

10.1 A command slice: CreateUser

src/Sentinel.Application/Users/CreateUser/CreateUserCommand.cs 
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Validation;
using Sentinel.Domain.Users;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Users.CreateUser;

public sealed record CreateUserCommand(string Email, string DisplayName, string TimeZoneId) : ICommand<Guid>;

internal sealed class CreateUserCommandValidator : Validator<CreateUserCommand>
{
    public override IEnumerable<ValidationFailure> Validate(CreateUserCommand request) =>
        Required(request.Email, nameof(request.Email))
            .Concat(MaxLength(request.Email, EmailAddress.MaxLength, nameof(request.Email)))
            .Concat(Required(request.DisplayName, nameof(request.DisplayName)))
            .Concat(MaxLength(request.DisplayName, User.MaxDisplayNameLength, nameof(request.DisplayName)))
            .Concat(Required(request.TimeZoneId, nameof(request.TimeZoneId)));
}
src/Sentinel.Application/Users/CreateUser/CreateUserCommandHandler.cs 
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Ports;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;
using Sentinel.Domain.Users;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Users.CreateUser;

internal sealed class CreateUserCommandHandler(IApplicationDbContext db, IClock clock)
    : ICommandHandler<CreateUserCommand, Guid>
{
    public async Task<Result<Guid>> Handle(CreateUserCommand request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var email = EmailAddress.Create(request.Email);
        if (email.IsFailure)
            return email.Error!;

        // The unique index is the real guarantee; this check exists to turn
        // the common case into a friendly 409 instead of a database exception.
        if (await db.Users.AnyAsync(u => u.Email == email.Value, cancellationToken))
            return UserErrors.DuplicateEmail(email.Value);

        var user = User.Create(email.Value, request.DisplayName, request.TimeZoneId, clock.UtcNow);
        if (user.IsFailure)
            return user.Error!;

        db.Users.Add(user.Value);
        await db.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);

        return user.Value.Id;
    }
}

The shape every command handler follows:

  1. Turn primitives into domain values (EmailAddress.Create); return the error if that fails.
  2. Check what needs the database (duplicate email).
  3. Ask the domain to do the work (User.Create).
  4. Save; return the id.

The comment about the unique index matters. The AnyAsync check is a courtesy that turns the common case into a friendly 409; under concurrency, two requests can both pass it, and only the database’s unique index stops the second. Never let an application-level check be the only guarantee of uniqueness.

10.2 Commands that change an aggregate

src/Sentinel.Application/Users/RoleAssignment/RoleAssignmentHandlers.cs 
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Ports;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;
using Sentinel.Domain.Roles;
using Sentinel.Domain.Users;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Users.RoleAssignment;

// Assign and revoke are two halves of one use case and change for the same
// reasons, so they share a slice. Two handlers, still one responsibility each.

internal sealed class AssignRoleCommandHandler(IApplicationDbContext db, IClock clock) : ICommandHandler<AssignRoleCommand>
{
    public async Task<Result> Handle(AssignRoleCommand request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var user = await db.Users.FirstOrDefaultAsync(u => u.Id == request.UserId, cancellationToken);
        if (user is null)
            return UserErrors.NotFound(request.UserId);

        if (!await db.Roles.AnyAsync(r => r.Id == request.RoleId, cancellationToken))
            return RoleErrors.NotFound(request.RoleId);

        var result = user.AssignRole(request.RoleId, clock.UtcNow);
        if (result.IsFailure)
            return result;

        await db.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
        return Result.Success();
    }
}

internal sealed class RevokeRoleCommandHandler(IApplicationDbContext db) : ICommandHandler<RevokeRoleCommand>
{
    public async Task<Result> Handle(RevokeRoleCommand request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var user = await db.Users.FirstOrDefaultAsync(u => u.Id == request.UserId, cancellationToken);
        if (user is null)
            return UserErrors.NotFound(request.UserId);

        var result = user.RevokeRole(request.RoleId);
        if (result.IsFailure)
            return result;

        await db.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
        return Result.Success();
    }
}

Load, call one method, save. All the rules are in User.AssignRole; the handler only checks the thing the aggregate cannot know (whether the role exists).

10.3 The access slices

All three share one helper, so that “how a user becomes an AccessSubject” cannot drift between screens:

src/Sentinel.Application/Access/AccessSubjectLoader.cs 
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Ports;
using Sentinel.Domain.Access;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Access;

/// <summary>
/// Loads what <see cref="PageAccessEvaluator"/> needs to know about a user.
/// Shared by every slice that answers "what may this person see?", which is
/// the one place sharing between slices is worth its coupling: the rule
/// "how a user becomes an AccessSubject" must not drift between screens.
/// </summary>
internal static class AccessSubjectLoader
{
    /// <returns>The subject, or null when <paramref name="userId"/> names no user.</returns>
    public static async Task<AccessSubject?> LoadAccessSubjectAsync(
        this IApplicationDbContext db, Guid? userId, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        if (userId is null)
            return AccessSubject.Anonymous;

        var user = await db.Users
            .AsNoTracking()
            .FirstOrDefaultAsync(u => u.Id == userId, cancellationToken);

        if (user is null)
            return null;

        var roleIds = user.RoleIds.ToList();
        var roles = await db.Roles
            .AsNoTracking()
            .Where(r => roleIds.Contains(r.Id))
            .ToListAsync(cancellationToken);

        return AccessSubject.For(user, roles);
    }
}

Check one page (used by the Angular route guard on every navigation):

src/Sentinel.Application/Pages/CheckPageAccess/CheckPageAccessQuery.cs 
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Validation;
using Sentinel.Contracts;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Pages.CheckPageAccess;

/// <summary>
/// May this user open this one page? The Angular route guard asks this
/// before every navigation, so a hand-typed URL is checked as carefully as
/// a click on the menu.
/// </summary>
public sealed record CheckPageAccessQuery(Guid? UserId, string Path) : IQuery<PageAccessDto>;

internal sealed class CheckPageAccessQueryValidator : Validator<CheckPageAccessQuery>
{
    public override IEnumerable<ValidationFailure> Validate(CheckPageAccessQuery request) =>
        Required(request.Path, nameof(request.Path))
            .Concat(MaxLength(request.Path, 200, nameof(request.Path)));
}
src/Sentinel.Application/Pages/CheckPageAccess/CheckPageAccessQueryHandler.cs 
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Ports;
using Sentinel.Application.Access;
using Sentinel.Contracts;
using Sentinel.Domain.Access;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;
using Sentinel.Domain.Pages;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Pages.CheckPageAccess;

internal sealed class CheckPageAccessQueryHandler(IApplicationDbContext db) : IQueryHandler<CheckPageAccessQuery, PageAccessDto>
{
    public async Task<Result<PageAccessDto>> Handle(CheckPageAccessQuery request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var subject = await db.LoadAccessSubjectAsync(request.UserId, cancellationToken) ?? AccessSubject.Anonymous;

        // The whole tree is needed even for one page: the answer depends on
        // every ancestor. Sentinel has tens of pages, not thousands; Chapter 10
        // discusses what to do when that stops being true.
        var pages = await db.Pages.AsNoTracking().ToListAsync(cancellationToken);

        var decision = PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluatePath(subject, pages, request.Path);
        if (decision is null)
            return PageErrors.NotFound(request.Path);

        return decision.ToDto(pages.ToDictionary(p => p.Id));
    }
}

The menu for the current user:

src/Sentinel.Application/Pages/GetNavigation/GetNavigationQueryHandler.cs 
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Ports;
using Sentinel.Application.Access;
using Sentinel.Contracts;
using Sentinel.Domain.Access;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Pages.GetNavigation;

internal sealed class GetNavigationQueryHandler(IApplicationDbContext db) : IQueryHandler<GetNavigationQuery, IReadOnlyList<NavigationNodeDto>>
{
    public async Task<Result<IReadOnlyList<NavigationNodeDto>>> Handle(GetNavigationQuery request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        // An id that names no user (deleted since the token was issued) is
        // treated as anonymous rather than as an error: the menu should
        // degrade to the public pages, not fail to render.
        var subject = await db.LoadAccessSubjectAsync(request.UserId, cancellationToken) ?? AccessSubject.Anonymous;

        var pages = await db.Pages.AsNoTracking().ToListAsync(cancellationToken);

        return Result.Success(PageAccessEvaluator.EvaluateAll(subject, pages).ToNavigationTree());
    }
}

Note the edge case in the comment: a user id that no longer exists (deleted since the token was issued) degrades to the public menu rather than failing.

Every page with its verdict for one user, for the admin access explorer:

src/Sentinel.Application/Pages/GetPageAccess/GetPageAccessQueryHandler.cs 
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Ports;
using Sentinel.Application.Access;
using Sentinel.Contracts;
using Sentinel.Domain.Access;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;
using Sentinel.Domain.Users;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Pages.GetPageAccess;

internal sealed class GetPageAccessQueryHandler(IApplicationDbContext db) : IQueryHandler<GetPageAccessQuery, IReadOnlyList<PageAccessDto>>
{
    public async Task<Result<IReadOnlyList<PageAccessDto>>> Handle(GetPageAccessQuery request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var subject = await db.LoadAccessSubjectAsync(request.UserId, cancellationToken);
        if (subject is null)
            return UserErrors.NotFound(request.UserId);

        var pages = await db.Pages.AsNoTracking().OrderBy(p => p.Path).ToListAsync(cancellationToken);
        var pagesById = pages.ToDictionary(p => p.Id);

        IReadOnlyList<PageAccessDto> result = PageAccessEvaluator
            .EvaluateAll(subject, pages)
            .Select(d => d.ToDto(pagesById))
            .ToList();

        return Result.Success(result);
    }
}

The mapping from decisions to DTOs, including building the menu tree:

src/Sentinel.Application/Pages/PageAccessMapping.cs 
using Sentinel.Contracts;
using Sentinel.Domain.Access;
using Sentinel.Domain.Pages;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Pages;

/// <summary>Turns evaluator decisions into the shapes the three page-access slices return.</summary>
internal static class PageAccessMapping
{
    public static PageAccessDto ToDto(this PageAccessDecision decision, IReadOnlyDictionary<Guid, Page> pagesById)
    {
        var page = decision.Page;
        var parentPath = page.ParentId is { } parentId && pagesById.TryGetValue(parentId, out var parent)
            ? parent.Path
            : null;

        return new PageAccessDto(
            page.Path,
            page.Title,
            parentPath,
            page.RequiredPermission?.Value,
            decision.IsAllowed,
            decision.Reason.ToString());
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Builds the menu from the allowed pages. A public page whose parent is
    /// hidden is promoted to the top level rather than dropped: the evaluator
    /// said the user may open it, so the menu must offer a way to get there.
    /// </summary>
    public static IReadOnlyList<NavigationNodeDto> ToNavigationTree(this IEnumerable<PageAccessDecision> decisions)
    {
        var allowed = decisions.Where(d => d.IsAllowed).Select(d => d.Page).ToList();
        var allowedIds = allowed.Select(p => p.Id).ToHashSet();

        var childrenByParent = allowed
            .Where(p => p.ParentId is { } id && allowedIds.Contains(id))
            .ToLookup(p => p.ParentId!.Value);

        var roots = allowed.Where(p => p.ParentId is not { } id || !allowedIds.Contains(id));

        return Build(roots, childrenByParent);
    }

    private static List<NavigationNodeDto> Build(IEnumerable<Page> pages, ILookup<Guid, Page> childrenByParent) =>
        pages
            .OrderBy(p => p.SortOrder)
            .ThenBy(p => p.Title, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            .Select(p => new NavigationNodeDto(p.Path, p.Title, Build(childrenByParent[p.Id], childrenByParent)))
            .ToList();
}

ToNavigationTree handles the edge case from §7.1: a public page under a hidden parent is promoted to the top level. The evaluator said the user may open it, so the menu must offer a way to get there.

Guarding endpoints with the same rules:

src/Sentinel.Application/Access/HasPermission/HasPermissionQueryHandler.cs 
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Ports;
using Sentinel.Domain.Access;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;
using Sentinel.Domain.Users;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Access.HasPermission;

internal sealed class HasPermissionQueryHandler(IApplicationDbContext db) : IQueryHandler<HasPermissionQuery, bool>
{
    public async Task<Result<bool>> Handle(HasPermissionQuery request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var permission = Permission.Create(request.Permission);
        if (permission.IsFailure)
            return permission.Error!;

        var subject = await db.LoadAccessSubjectAsync(request.UserId, cancellationToken);
        if (subject is null)
            return UserErrors.NotFound(request.UserId);

        return subject.Has(permission.Value);
    }
}

10.4 The security slices

The status query, the history query and the acknowledge command must agree on what the findings are, so they share an assessor:

src/Sentinel.Application/Security/AccountAssessor.cs 
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Ports;
using Sentinel.Domain.Security;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Security;

internal sealed record AccountAssessment(
    SecurityAssessment Assessment,
    IReadOnlyList<SignInAttempt> History,
    DateTime AssessedAtUtc)
{
    /// <summary>Ids of every attempt cited as evidence by an unacknowledged finding.</summary>
    public IReadOnlySet<Guid> FlaggedAttemptIds { get; } =
        Assessment.Findings.SelectMany(f => f.AttemptIds).ToHashSet();
}

/// <summary>
/// Loads a user's history and runs the detector over it. Shared by the
