13.2 Handlers against SQLite

tests/Sentinel.Application.Tests/TestHost.cs 
using Microsoft.Data.Sqlite;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Sentinel.Application;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Ports;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;
using Sentinel.Infrastructure.Persistence;
using Sentinel.Infrastructure.Persistence.Seeding;
using Sentinel.Infrastructure.Services;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Tests;

public sealed class FakeClock(DateTime utcNow) : IClock
{
    public DateTime UtcNow { get; set; } = utcNow;
}

/// <summary>
/// The real Application layer and the real EF Core model, over an in-memory
/// SQLite database that lives as long as this object. Handlers run through
/// the real dispatcher and pipeline, so a test here exercises exactly what an
/// endpoint would, minus HTTP.
/// </summary>
/// <remarks>
/// SQLite is not SQL Server. It is close enough for the queries in this book,
/// and the differences that matter (case sensitivity, mainly) are handled
/// explicitly in the handlers. Run the API tests against SQL Server in CI if
/// your queries grow provider-specific.
/// </remarks>
public sealed class TestHost : IAsyncDisposable
{
    public static readonly DateTime Now = new(2026, 10, 25, 12, 0, 0, DateTimeKind.Utc);

    private readonly SqliteConnection _connection;
    private readonly ServiceProvider _services;

    private TestHost(SqliteConnection connection, ServiceProvider services)
    {
        _connection = connection;
        _services = services;
    }

    public FakeClock Clock => (FakeClock)_services.GetRequiredService<IClock>();

    public static async Task<TestHost> CreateAsync(bool seed = false)
    {
        // The database exists for as long as one connection to it is open.
        var connection = new SqliteConnection("DataSource=:memory:");
        await connection.OpenAsync();

        var services = new ServiceCollection();
        services.AddLogging();
        services.AddApplication();
        services.AddDbContext<SentinelDbContext>(o => o.UseSqlite(connection));
        services.AddScoped<IApplicationDbContext>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<SentinelDbContext>());
        services.AddSingleton<IClock>(new FakeClock(Now));
        services.AddSingleton<IGeoLocator, StaticGeoLocator>();
        services.AddScoped<DevelopmentDataSeeder>();

        var host = new TestHost(connection, services.BuildServiceProvider(validateScopes: true));

        await using var scope = host._services.CreateAsyncScope();
        var db = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<SentinelDbContext>();
        await db.Database.EnsureCreatedAsync();
        if (seed)
            await scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<DevelopmentDataSeeder>().SeedAsync();

        return host;
    }

    /// <summary>Sends a request in its own scope, like one HTTP request would.</summary>
    public async Task<TResponse> Send<TResponse>(IRequest<TResponse> request) where TResponse : Result
    {
        await using var scope = _services.CreateAsyncScope();
        return await scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IDispatcher>().Send(request);
    }

    /// <summary>A fresh context, so assertions read what was saved rather than what is cached.</summary>
    public async Task<T> Query<T>(Func<SentinelDbContext, Task<T>> query)
    {
        await using var scope = _services.CreateAsyncScope();
        return await query(scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<SentinelDbContext>());
    }

    public async Task<Guid> UserIdAsync(string email) =>
        await Query(db => db.Users.Where(u => u.Email == Domain.Users.EmailAddress.Create(email).Value).Select(u => u.Id).SingleAsync());

    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()
    {
        await _services.DisposeAsync();
        await _connection.DisposeAsync();
    }
}

The host runs the real dispatcher, the real pipeline and the real EF Core model, over an in-memory SQLite database that lives as long as the connection is open. Each Send gets its own DI scope, as an HTTP request would, so a test cannot accidentally pass because two operations shared a change tracker.

tests/Sentinel.Application.Tests/SecuritySliceTests.cs 
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Sentinel.Application.Security;
using Sentinel.Application.Security.AcknowledgeFinding;
using Sentinel.Application.Security.GetAccountSecurityStatus;
using Sentinel.Application.Security.GetSignInHistory;
using Sentinel.Application.Security.RecordSignIn;
using Sentinel.Application.Users.CreateUser;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Tests;

public class SecuritySliceTests
{
    [Theory]
    [InlineData("ada.okafor@sentinel.dev", "Low")]
    [InlineData("bola.adeyemi@sentinel.dev", "High")]
    [InlineData("chen.wei@sentinel.dev", "Medium")]
    [InlineData("dana.smith@sentinel.dev", "Medium")]
    [InlineData("emeka.nwosu@sentinel.dev", "None")]
    [InlineData("tunde.bakare@sentinel.dev", "High")]
    public async Task Each_seeded_story_produces_its_risk_level(string email, string expected)
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);

        var status = (await host.Send(new GetAccountSecurityStatusQuery(await host.UserIdAsync(email)))).Value;

        Assert.Equal(expected, status.RiskLevel);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Regression test for SUP-4219 (Chapter 23). Tunde has more sign-ins than
    /// the assessor loads. If the query takes the oldest rows instead of the
    /// newest, yesterday's attack is never seen and the page says "all clear".
    /// </summary>
    [Fact]
    public async Task When_history_exceeds_the_cap_the_newest_attempts_are_assessed()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);
        var tunde = await host.UserIdAsync("tunde.bakare@sentinel.dev");
        var total = await host.Query(db => db.SignInAttempts.CountAsync(a => a.UserId == tunde));
        Assert.True(total > AccountAssessor.MaxHistory, "The seed data must exceed the cap for this test to mean anything.");

        var status = (await host.Send(new GetAccountSecurityStatusQuery(tunde))).Value;

        Assert.Contains(status.Findings, f => f.Kind == "BruteForce" && f.Severity == "High");
        Assert.Equal(status.RecentSignIns.Max(s => s.OccurredAtUtc), status.RecentSignIns[0].OccurredAtUtc);
    }

    /// <summary>Regression test for SUP-4172 (Chapter 22): what comes back from the database is UTC.</summary>
    [Fact]
    public async Task Sign_in_times_come_back_from_the_database_as_utc()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);

        var status = (await host.Send(new GetAccountSecurityStatusQuery(await host.UserIdAsync("ada.okafor@sentinel.dev")))).Value;

        Assert.All(status.RecentSignIns, s => Assert.Equal(DateTimeKind.Utc, s.OccurredAtUtc.Kind));
        Assert.All(status.Findings, f => Assert.Equal(DateTimeKind.Utc, f.OccurredAtUtc.Kind));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Flagged_rows_are_exactly_the_evidence_for_the_findings()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);

        var status = (await host.Send(new GetAccountSecurityStatusQuery(await host.UserIdAsync("bola.adeyemi@sentinel.dev")))).Value;

        var evidence = status.Findings.SelectMany(f => f.AttemptIds).ToHashSet();
        Assert.All(status.RecentSignIns, s => Assert.Equal(evidence.Contains(s.Id), s.IsFlagged));
        Assert.Contains(status.RecentSignIns, s => s.IsFlagged);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Acknowledging_a_finding_lowers_the_risk_and_is_idempotent()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);
        var dana = await host.UserIdAsync("dana.smith@sentinel.dev");
        var before = (await host.Send(new GetAccountSecurityStatusQuery(dana))).Value;
        var newCountry = before.Findings.Single(f => f.Kind == "NewCountry");

        Assert.True((await host.Send(new AcknowledgeFindingCommand(dana, newCountry.Key))).IsSuccess);
        Assert.True((await host.Send(new AcknowledgeFindingCommand(dana, newCountry.Key))).IsSuccess);

        var after = (await host.Send(new GetAccountSecurityStatusQuery(dana))).Value;
        Assert.Equal("Medium", before.RiskLevel);
        Assert.Equal("Low", after.RiskLevel);
        Assert.False(after.IsCompromiseSuspected);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task A_finding_the_user_cannot_see_cannot_be_acknowledged()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);
        var dana = await host.UserIdAsync("dana.smith@sentinel.dev");

        var result = await host.Send(new AcknowledgeFindingCommand(dana, "brute-force:made-up"));

        Assert.Equal(ErrorType.NotFound, result.Error!.Type);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Recording_a_sign_in_resolves_the_location_and_stores_utc()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync();
        await host.Send(new CreateUserCommand("ada@example.com", "Ada", "Africa/Lagos"));

        // 13:00 in Lagos is 12:00 UTC.
        var lagosTime = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 10, 25, 13, 0, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(1));
        var id = (await host.Send(new RecordSignInCommand("ada@example.com", lagosTime, "102.89.34.7", "curl/8", true, null))).Value;

        var saved = await host.Query(db => db.SignInAttempts.SingleAsync(a => a.Id == id));
        Assert.Equal(new DateTime(2026, 10, 25, 12, 0, 0, DateTimeKind.Utc), saved.OccurredAtUtc);
        Assert.Equal(DateTimeKind.Utc, saved.OccurredAtUtc.Kind);
        Assert.Equal("Lagos, NG", saved.Location.ToString());
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Sign_ins_from_the_future_and_for_unknown_users_are_rejected()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync();
        await host.Send(new CreateUserCommand("ada@example.com", "Ada", "Africa/Lagos"));
        var tomorrow = new DateTimeOffset(TestHost.Now.AddDays(1));

        Assert.Equal("SignIn.InFuture", (await host.Send(new RecordSignInCommand("ada@example.com", tomorrow, "1.1.1.1", null, true, null))).Error!.Code);
        Assert.Equal(ErrorType.NotFound, (await host.Send(new RecordSignInCommand("who@example.com", TestHost.Now, "1.1.1.1", null, true, null))).Error!.Type);
        Assert.Equal(ErrorType.Validation, (await host.Send(new RecordSignInCommand("ada@example.com", TestHost.Now, "1.1.1.1", null, false, "Bananas"))).Error!.Type);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task History_is_paged_newest_first()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);
        var tunde = await host.UserIdAsync("tunde.bakare@sentinel.dev");

        var first = (await host.Send(new GetSignInHistoryQuery(tunde, 1, 10))).Value;
        var second = (await host.Send(new GetSignInHistoryQuery(tunde, 2, 10))).Value;

        Assert.Equal(10, first.Items.Count);
        Assert.True(first.Items[^1].OccurredAtUtc >= second.Items[0].OccurredAtUtc);
        Assert.Equal(first.Items.OrderByDescending(i => i.OccurredAtUtc).Select(i => i.Id), first.Items.Select(i => i.Id));
        Assert.True(first.TotalCount > 500);
    }
}

Two tests here are labelled as regression tests for the incidents in Part IV. On the lab branches they are deleted, because the point of a lab is that the bug shipped: the test did not exist.

tests/Sentinel.Application.Tests/PageAccessSliceTests.cs 
using Sentinel.Application.Pages.CheckPageAccess;
using Sentinel.Application.Pages.CreatePage;
using Sentinel.Application.Pages.GetNavigation;
using Sentinel.Application.Pages.GetPageAccess;
using Sentinel.Application.Roles.GetRoles;
using Sentinel.Application.Roles.RolePermissions;
using Sentinel.Application.Users.RoleAssignment;
using Sentinel.Contracts;
using Sentinel.Domain.Common;

namespace Sentinel.Application.Tests;

public class PageAccessSliceTests
{
    private static IEnumerable<string> Flatten(IEnumerable<NavigationNodeDto> nodes) =>
        nodes.SelectMany(n => Flatten(n.Children).Prepend(n.Path));

    [Fact]
    public async Task The_menu_contains_exactly_the_allowed_pages()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);
        var emeka = await host.UserIdAsync("emeka.nwosu@sentinel.dev");

        var menu = (await host.Send(new GetNavigationQuery(emeka))).Value;

        Assert.Equal(
            ["/", "/account", "/account/security", "/reports", "/reports/finance", "/billing", "/help", "/status"],
            Flatten(menu));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Anonymous_visitors_get_the_public_pages()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);

        var menu = (await host.Send(new GetNavigationQuery(null))).Value;

        Assert.Equal(["/help", "/status"], Flatten(menu));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task An_explicit_deny_is_explained()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);
        var emeka = await host.UserIdAsync("emeka.nwosu@sentinel.dev");

        var verdict = (await host.Send(new CheckPageAccessQuery(emeka, "/reports/finance/export"))).Value;

        Assert.False(verdict.IsAllowed);
        Assert.Equal("ExplicitlyDenied", verdict.Reason);
        Assert.Equal("/reports/finance", verdict.ParentPath);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Checking_an_unknown_page_is_not_found()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);

        var result = await host.Send(new CheckPageAccessQuery(null, "/nowhere"));

        Assert.Equal(ErrorType.NotFound, result.Error!.Type);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task The_access_explorer_lists_every_page_with_a_reason()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);
        var grace = await host.UserIdAsync("grace.eze@sentinel.dev"); // suspended

        var rows = (await host.Send(new GetPageAccessQuery(grace))).Value;

        Assert.Equal(15, rows.Count);
        Assert.All(rows.Where(r => !r.IsAllowed), r => Assert.Equal("UserSuspended", r.Reason));
        Assert.Equal(["/help", "/status"], rows.Where(r => r.IsAllowed).Select(r => r.Path));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Granting_a_role_permission_is_saved_and_changes_access()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);
        var chen = await host.UserIdAsync("chen.wei@sentinel.dev");
        var operations = (await host.Send(new GetRolesQuery())).Value.Single(r => r.Name == "Operations");

        Assert.False((await host.Send(new CheckPageAccessQuery(chen, "/billing"))).Value.IsAllowed);

        Assert.True((await host.Send(new GrantPermissionCommand(operations.Id, "billing.view"))).IsSuccess);

        // A fresh scope reads from the database: proves the value comparer
        // noticed the list changed and EF Core actually wrote it.
        Assert.True((await host.Send(new CheckPageAccessQuery(chen, "/billing"))).Value.IsAllowed);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Revoking_a_role_removes_its_pages()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);
        var femi = await host.UserIdAsync("femi.bello@sentinel.dev");
        var auditor = (await host.Send(new GetRolesQuery())).Value.Single(r => r.Name == "Auditor");

        await host.Send(new RevokeRoleCommand(femi, auditor.Id));

        var menu = Flatten((await host.Send(new GetNavigationQuery(femi))).Value).ToList();
        Assert.DoesNotContain("/admin", menu);
        Assert.DoesNotContain("/reports", menu);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Pages_cannot_require_a_wildcard()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);

        var result = await host.Send(new CreatePageCommand("/reports/all", "All", "/reports", "reports.*", false, 0));

        Assert.Equal("Page.WildcardPermission", result.Error!.Code);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task A_new_page_must_have_an_existing_parent_and_a_unique_path()
    {
        await using var host = await TestHost.CreateAsync(seed: true);

        Assert.Equal(ErrorType.NotFound, (await host.Send(new CreatePageCommand("/x/y", "Y", "/x", null, false, 0))).Error!.Type);
        Assert.Equal(ErrorType.Conflict, (await host.Send(new CreatePageCommand("/Billing/", "Again", "/", null, false, 0))).Error!.Type);
        Assert.True((await host.Send(new CreatePageCommand("/billing/invoices", "Invoices", "/billing", "billing.view", false, 0))).IsSuccess);
    }
}

tests/Sentinel.Api.Tests/SentinelApiFactory.cs 
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;
using Microsoft.Data.Sqlite;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Infrastructure;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting;
using Sentinel.Api.Authentication;
using Sentinel.Infrastructure.Persistence;
using Sentinel.Infrastructure.Persistence.Seeding;

namespace Sentinel.Api.Tests;

/// <summary>
/// The whole API, in process, over an in-memory SQLite database seeded with
/// the development data. One factory per test class (xUnit's class fixture),
/// so tests in a class share a database: write tests that do not depend on
/// each other's changes.
/// </summary>
public sealed class SentinelApiFactory : WebApplicationFactory<Program>
{
    private readonly SqliteConnection _connection = new("DataSource=:memory:");

    protected override void ConfigureWebHost(IWebHostBuilder builder)
    {
        _connection.Open();

        builder.UseEnvironment("Development");

        // The migrations are SQL Server's. Tests build the schema from the model instead.
        builder.UseSetting("Database:MigrateAndSeedOnStartup", "false");

        builder.ConfigureServices(services =>
        {
            services.RemoveAll<DbContextOptions<SentinelDbContext>>();
            services.RemoveAll(typeof(IDbContextOptionsConfiguration<SentinelDbContext>));
            services.AddDbContext<SentinelDbContext>(o => o.UseSqlite(_connection));
        });
    }

    protected override IHost CreateHost(IHostBuilder builder)
    {
        var host = base.CreateHost(builder);

        using var scope = host.Services.CreateScope();
        scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<SentinelDbContext>().Database.EnsureCreated();
        scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<DevelopmentDataSeeder>().SeedAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult();

        return host;
    }

    /// <summary>A client signed in as <paramref name="email"/>, or anonymous when null.</summary>
    public HttpClient ClientFor(string? email)
    {
        var client = CreateClient();
        if (email is not null)
            client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Add(DemoUserAuthenticationHandler.HeaderName, email);
        client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Accept.Add(new MediaTypeWithQualityHeaderValue("application/json"));
        return client;
    }

    protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)
    {
        base.Dispose(disposing);
        if (disposing)
            _connection.Dispose();
    }
}

WebApplicationFactory<Program> hosts the real API in memory. The factory swaps SQL Server for SQLite (removing both the options and EF Core 9+’s IDbContextOptionsConfiguration<T> registrations; removing only the first leaves SQL Server configured), turns off start-up migration, and seeds.

tests/Sentinel.Api.Tests/ApiTests.cs 
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Json;
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using Sentinel.Contracts;

namespace Sentinel.Api.Tests;

public partial class ApiTests(SentinelApiFactory factory) : IClassFixture<SentinelApiFactory>
{
    private const string Ada = "ada.okafor@sentinel.dev";      // Administrator
    private const string Femi = "femi.bello@sentinel.dev";     // Auditor: admin.users, not .manage
    private const string Chen = "chen.wei@sentinel.dev";       // Operations
    private const string Dana = "dana.smith@sentinel.dev";

    // ---- Authentication ----

    [Fact]
    public async Task Me_requires_authentication()
    {
        var response = await factory.ClientFor(null).GetAsync("/api/me");

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, response.StatusCode);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task An_unknown_demo_user_is_not_authenticated()
    {
        var response = await factory.ClientFor("nobody@example.com").GetAsync("/api/me");

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, response.StatusCode);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Me_returns_the_signed_in_user()
    {
        var me = await factory.ClientFor(Ada).GetFromJsonAsync<CurrentUserDto>("/api/me");

        Assert.Equal("Ada Okafor", me!.DisplayName);
        Assert.Equal("Africa/Lagos", me.TimeZoneId);
        Assert.Equal(["*"], me.Permissions);
    }

    // ---- Authorisation: the endpoint, not just the menu ----

    [Theory]
    [InlineData(Ada, "/api/users", HttpStatusCode.OK)]
    [InlineData(Femi, "/api/users", HttpStatusCode.OK)]
    [InlineData(Chen, "/api/users", HttpStatusCode.Forbidden)]
    [InlineData(Femi, "/api/roles", HttpStatusCode.Forbidden)] // auditors see users, not roles
    public async Task Admin_reads_are_guarded_by_permission(string user, string url, HttpStatusCode expected)
    {
        var response = await factory.ClientFor(user).GetAsync(url);

        Assert.Equal(expected, response.StatusCode);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Reading_a_resource_does_not_imply_changing_it()
    {
        var response = await factory.ClientFor(Femi).PostAsJsonAsync("/api/users",
            new CreateUserRequest("new@sentinel.dev", "New", "Africa/Lagos"));

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Forbidden, response.StatusCode);
    }

    // ---- Results to HTTP ----

    [Fact]
    public async Task Validation_errors_are_a_400_problem_with_one_entry_per_field()
    {
        var response = await factory.ClientFor(Ada).PostAsJsonAsync("/api/users", new CreateUserRequest("", "", "Africa/Lagos"));

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.BadRequest, response.StatusCode);
        using var problem = JsonDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
        var errors = problem.RootElement.GetProperty("errors");
        Assert.True(errors.TryGetProperty("Email", out _));
        Assert.True(errors.TryGetProperty("DisplayName", out _));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Business_rule_failures_carry_their_error_code()
    {
        var response = await factory.ClientFor(Ada).PostAsJsonAsync("/api/users",
            new CreateUserRequest("someone@sentinel.dev", "Someone", "Mars/Base"));

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.BadRequest, response.StatusCode);
        using var problem = JsonDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
        Assert.Equal("User.UnknownTimeZone", problem.RootElement.GetProperty("code").GetString());
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Creating_a_user_returns_201_with_a_location()
    {
        var response = await factory.ClientFor(Ada).PostAsJsonAsync("/api/users",
            new CreateUserRequest("kemi.ade@sentinel.dev", "Kemi Ade", "Africa/Lagos"));

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Created, response.StatusCode);
        var created = await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<CreatedResponse>();
        Assert.Equal($"/api/users/{created!.Id}", response.Headers.Location!.OriginalString);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Unknown_ids_are_404()
    {
        var response = await factory.ClientFor(Ada).GetAsync($"/api/users/{Guid.NewGuid()}");

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.NotFound, response.StatusCode);
    }

    // ---- Page access over HTTP ----

    [Fact]
    public async Task Anonymous_navigation_is_the_public_pages()
    {
        var menu = await factory.ClientFor(null).GetFromJsonAsync<List<NavigationNodeDto>>("/api/me/navigation");

        Assert.Equal(["/help", "/status"], menu!.Select(n => n.Path));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task The_guard_endpoint_explains_a_denial()
    {
        var verdict = await factory.ClientFor(Chen).GetFromJsonAsync<PageAccessDto>("/api/me/page-access?path=/admin/users");

        Assert.False(verdict!.IsAllowed);
        Assert.Equal("ParentDenied", verdict.Reason);
    }

    // ---- The wire format for dates (SUP-4172, Chapter 22) ----

    [Fact]
    public async Task Every_timestamp_on_the_wire_is_utc_with_a_z()
    {
        var json = await factory.ClientFor(Dana).GetStringAsync("/api/me/security");

        var timestamps = TimestampProperty().Matches(json).Select(m => m.Groups["value"].Value).ToList();

        Assert.NotEmpty(timestamps);
        Assert.All(timestamps, t => Assert.EndsWith("Z", t));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Acknowledging_a_finding_over_http_returns_204_and_lowers_the_risk()
    {
        var client = factory.ClientFor(Dana);
        var before = await client.GetFromJsonAsync<AccountSecurityStatusDto>("/api/me/security");
        var finding = before!.Findings.First(f => f.Kind == "NewDevice");

        var response = await client.PostAsync($"/api/me/security/findings/{Uri.EscapeDataString(finding.Key)}/acknowledge", null);

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.NoContent, response.StatusCode);
        var after = await client.GetFromJsonAsync<AccountSecurityStatusDto>("/api/me/security");
        Assert.DoesNotContain(after!.Findings, f => f.Key == finding.Key);
    }

    [GeneratedRegex("\"(occurredAtUtc|assessedAtUtc)\":\"(?<value>[^\"]+)\"")]
    private static partial Regex TimestampProperty();
}

Every_timestamp_on_the_wire_is_utc_with_a_z is the test that would have prevented Chapter 22. It reads the raw JSON, not a deserialised object, because deserialising would hide the very thing it is checking.

13.4 Architecture tests

tests/Sentinel.Architecture.Tests/DependencyRuleTests.cs 
using System.Reflection;
using Sentinel.Application.Abstractions.Messaging;

namespace Sentinel.Architecture.Tests;

/// <summary>
/// The dependency rule, enforced by the build. A diagram in a wiki can be
/// ignored; a red test cannot. No NetArchTest package: reading referenced
/// assemblies and walking types is all it takes.
/// </summary>
public class DependencyRuleTests
{
    private static readonly Assembly Domain = typeof(Sentinel.Domain.Common.Result).Assembly;
    private static readonly Assembly Contracts = typeof(Sentinel.Contracts.PageDto).Assembly;
    private static readonly Assembly Application = typeof(IDispatcher).Assembly;
    private static readonly Assembly Infrastructure = typeof(Sentinel.Infrastructure.DependencyInjection).Assembly;
    private static readonly Assembly Api = typeof(Program).Assembly;

    private static IEnumerable<string> ReferencedNames(Assembly assembly) =>
        assembly.GetReferencedAssemblies().Select(a => a.Name!);

    private static bool IsFramework(string name) =>
        name is "netstandard" or "mscorlib" || name.StartsWith("System", StringComparison.Ordinal);

    [Fact]
    public void Domain_references_nothing_but_the_base_class_library()
    {
        var offenders = ReferencedNames(Domain).Where(n => !IsFramework(n)).ToList();

        Assert.Empty(offenders);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Contracts_reference_nothing_but_the_base_class_library()
    {
        Assert.DoesNotContain(ReferencedNames(Contracts), n => !IsFramework(n));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Application_does_not_know_about_infrastructure_or_the_web()
    {
        var names = ReferencedNames(Application).ToList();

        Assert.DoesNotContain("Sentinel.Infrastructure", names);
        Assert.DoesNotContain("Sentinel.Api", names);
        Assert.DoesNotContain(names, n => n.StartsWith("Microsoft.AspNetCore", StringComparison.Ordinal));
        Assert.DoesNotContain(names, n => n.StartsWith("Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer", StringComparison.Ordinal));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Infrastructure_does_not_know_about_the_web()
    {
        Assert.DoesNotContain("Sentinel.Api", ReferencedNames(Infrastructure));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Handlers_are_internal_so_only_the_dispatcher_can_call_them()
    {
        var publicHandlers = Application.GetTypes()
            .Where(t => t.IsClass && !t.IsAbstract)
            .Where(t => t.GetInterfaces().Any(i => i.IsGenericType && i.GetGenericTypeDefinition() == typeof(IRequestHandler<,>)))
            .Where(t => t.IsPublic)
            .Select(t => t.FullName)
            .ToList();

        Assert.Empty(publicHandlers);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Every_request_has_exactly_one_handler()
    {
        var requestTypes = Application.GetTypes()
            .Where(t => t is { IsClass: true, IsAbstract: false })
            .Where(t => t.GetInterfaces().Any(i => i.IsGenericType && i.GetGenericTypeDefinition() == typeof(IRequest<>)))
            .ToList();

        var handledTypes = Application.GetTypes()
            .SelectMany(t => t.GetInterfaces())
            .Where(i => i.IsGenericType && i.GetGenericTypeDefinition() == typeof(IRequestHandler<,>))
            .Select(i => i.GetGenericArguments()[0])
            .ToList();

        Assert.NotEmpty(requestTypes);
        Assert.All(requestTypes, r => Assert.Equal(1, handledTypes.Count(h => h == r)));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Requests_live_in_a_folder_of_their_own_named_after_the_feature()
    {
        // Vertical slices: Sentinel.Application.<Feature>.<UseCase>.<Request>.
        var misplaced = Application.GetTypes()
            .Where(t => t is { IsClass: true, IsAbstract: false })
            .Where(t => t.GetInterfaces().Any(i => i.IsGenericType && i.GetGenericTypeDefinition() == typeof(IRequest<>)))
            .Where(t => t.Namespace!.Split('.').Length != 4)
            .Select(t => t.FullName)
            .ToList();

        Assert.Empty(misplaced);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void The_api_references_the_layers_it_composes()
    {
        var names = ReferencedNames(Api).ToList();

        Assert.Contains("Sentinel.Application", names);
        Assert.Contains("Sentinel.Infrastructure", names);
    }
}

A diagram in a wiki can be ignored. A red build cannot. These tests also check two conventions: handlers are internal (only the dispatcher calls them) and every request has exactly one handler (a missing handler is otherwise a run-time exception on first use).

13.5 What not to test

Do not test EF Core, ASP.NET or the framework’s JSON serialiser. Test your decisions on top of them: that the converter makes dates UTC, not that EF can save a row. Do not write a test per getter. Do write a test for every decision you would have to explain to a reviewer.

Part III · The Angular Front End

Chapter 14 · Angular and TypeScript for the Test

The prep guide promises no trick questions about JavaScript and says the Angular scenario needs only basic reading and writing. “Basic” under a 25-minute timer means automatic. This chapter is the minimum you should be able to write without looking anything up.

14.1 The ES2015+ you will actually use

// const by default; let when it changes; never var.
const findings = status.findings;
let flaggedCount = 0;

// Arrow functions, and the array methods that replace most loops.
const high = findings.filter((f) => f.severity === 'High');
const keys = findings.map((f) => f.key);
const anyHigh = findings.some((f) => f.severity === 'High');
const total = signIns.reduce((sum, s) => sum + (s.succeeded ? 0 : 1), 0);

// Sorting: sort() mutates. Copy first, always.
const newestFirst = [...signIns].sort((a, b) => b.occurredAtUtc.localeCompare(a.occurredAtUtc));

// Destructuring and defaults.
const { riskLevel, findings: items = [] } = status;
function format(value: string, { locale = 'en-GB', showZone = true } = {}) { /* ... */ }

// Spread to copy and override (the builders in the specs do this).
const changed = { ...finding, severity: 'High' };

// Template literals.
const label = `Review ${count} ${count === 1 ? 'item' : 'items'}`;

// Optional chaining and nullish coalescing: different from || for 0 and ''.
const zone = user?.timeZoneId ?? 'UTC';

// Map and Set for lookups and "seen before".
const seenCountries = new Set<string>();
const byId = new Map(signIns.map((s) => [s.id, s]));

Two traps worth knowing because they cause real bugs, not because anyone will quiz you on them:

  • sort() without a comparator sorts as strings: [10, 9, 1].sort() is [1, 10, 9].
  • new Date('2026-10-24T08:00:00') with no Z is local time. Chapter 18 is about this.

14.2 TypeScript in one table

You want Write
A shape for API data interface SignInAttempt { id: string; succeeded: boolean; }
A closed set of strings type RiskLevel = 'None' \| 'Low' \| 'Medium' \| 'High';
One of several states a discriminated union: { kind: 'loading' } \| { kind: 'loaded'; status: X }
A lookup keyed by a union const titles: Record<FindingKind, string> = { ... }
“May be missing” string \| null (from JSON) or an optional ?: property
Narrowing if (state.kind === 'loaded') { state.status }

Concept Modern syntax (Angular 17+) What it is for

Appendix C translates every row into pre-17 syntax (@Input(), *ngIf, NgModule) in case the test environment is older.

14.4 RxJS: the six operators that cover most code

Operator Use
map Transform each value
switchMap Start a new request for each value, cancelling the previous one
catchError Turn an error into a value (an error state)
debounceTime Wait for typing to pause
distinctUntilChanged Ignore repeats
takeUntilDestroyed Unsubscribe when the component goes away

14.5 Using AI in the Angular scenario, properly

The third scenario encourages AI and asks you to cite it. Use it for what it is good at (syntax you have forgotten, an Intl option name, a test skeleton) and keep the decisions yours. Cite it the same way as any source:

// Relative time formatting adapted from an AI assistant's suggestion
// (ChatGPT, 2026-10-25, prompt: "Intl.RelativeTimeFormat days/hours ago").
// Reviewed and changed: "now" is a parameter so it can be tested.

What a reviewer cannot tell from AI-written code is whether you understood it. Your comments are where you show that you did.

Chapter 15 · The Angular Workspace and the Core Layer

15.1 Creating the workspace

mkdir client; cd client
npx @angular/cli@22 new sentinel-web --style=css --ssr=false --skip-git --routing `
  --package-manager=npm --ai-config=none --interactive=false
cd sentinel-web

Angular 22 creates a standalone, zoneless application tested with Vitest. Standalone means no NgModule: each component lists what it uses in its own imports. Zoneless means change detection is driven by signals and events rather than by Zone.js patching every timer; in practice it means “keep state in signals and the screen stays in step”.

File names have lost their suffixes in recent versions (app.ts rather than app.component.ts, class App rather than AppComponent). This book follows the current style guide.

15.2 Talking to the API through a proxy

The API runs on port 5080 and the dev server on 4200. Rather than enable CORS on the API, the dev server forwards /api to it:

client/sentinel-web/proxy.conf.json 
{
  "/api": {
    "target": "http://localhost:5080",
    "secure": false,
    "changeOrigin": true
  }
}

and angular.json points serve at that file ("options": { "proxyConfig": "proxy.conf.json" }). The browser only ever sees one origin, exactly as it will in production behind a reverse proxy.

If you write JSON files from Windows PowerShell 5 with Set-Content -Encoding utf8, they get a byte-order mark, and the Angular CLI then reports proxy.conf.json contains parse errors: [1, 1] InvalidSymbol. That happened while writing this chapter. The cure is to save without a BOM. Error positions like [1, 1] are a strong hint that the problem is invisible.

15.3 The models

client/sentinel-web/src/app/core/models/api-models.ts 
// Hand-written mirrors of src/Sentinel.Contracts. Keep the two in step:
// a property renamed in C# and not here compiles fine on both sides and
// fails silently at run time, as `undefined`.
//
// Timestamps arrive as ISO 8601 strings in UTC ("2026-10-24T08:00:00Z").
// They are deliberately typed `string`, not `Date`: JSON has no date type,
// and pretending otherwise hides the moment where parsing happens. Parse
// them with parseApiTimestamp() in core/time, never with `new Date()`.

/** An ISO 8601 UTC timestamp exactly as the API sent it. */
export type UtcTimestamp = string;

export type RiskLevel = 'None' | 'Low' | 'Medium' | 'High';
export type FindingKind = 'BruteForce' | 'ImpossibleTravel' | 'NewCountry' | 'NewDevice';

export interface CurrentUser {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  displayName: string;
  timeZoneId: string;
  permissions: string[];
}

export interface DemoUser {
  email: string;
  displayName: string;
  description: string;
}

export interface NavigationNode {
  path: string;
  title: string;
  children: NavigationNode[];
}

export type AccessReason =
  | 'PublicPage'
  | 'AuthenticatedUser'
  | 'PermissionGranted'
  | 'NotAuthenticated'
  | 'UserSuspended'
  | 'MissingPermission'
  | 'ExplicitlyDenied'
  | 'ParentDenied'
  | 'OrphanedPage'
  | 'CyclicHierarchy';

export interface PageAccess {
  path: string;
  title: string;
  parentPath: string | null;
  requiredPermission: string | null;
  isAllowed: boolean;
  reason: AccessReason;
}

export interface SignInAttempt {
  id: string;
  occurredAtUtc: UtcTimestamp;
  ipAddress: string;
  countryCode: string;
  city: string;
  device: string;
  succeeded: boolean;
  failureReason: string | null;
  isFlagged: boolean;
}

export interface SecurityFinding {
  key: string;
  kind: FindingKind;
  severity: RiskLevel;
  occurredAtUtc: UtcTimestamp;
  summary: string;
  attemptIds: string[];
}

export interface AccountSecurityStatus {
  riskLevel: RiskLevel;
  isCompromiseSuspected: boolean;
  assessedAtUtc: UtcTimestamp;
  timeZoneId: string;
  findings: SecurityFinding[];
  recentSignIns: SignInAttempt[];
}

export interface PagedResponse<T> {
  items: T[];
  page: number;
  pageSize: number;
  totalCount: number;
}

export interface UserSummary {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  displayName: string;
  status: 'Active' | 'Suspended';
  roles: string[];
}

export interface Role {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  description: string;
  permissions: string[];
  userCount: number;
}

Timestamps are typed string, on purpose. JSON has no date type, and declaring occurredAtUtc: Date would be a lie that the compiler believes: the value at run time would still be a string, and the moment it is parsed would be hidden. Here it is visible, and done in exactly one function (Chapter 18).

15.4 Errors, once

client/sentinel-web/src/app/core/http/api-error.ts 
import { HttpErrorResponse } from '@angular/common/http';

/**
 * Turns whatever an HTTP call threw into one sentence a user can read.
 *
 * The API answers failures with RFC 9457 problem details
 * (`{ title, detail, status, errors? }`), but a failure can also come from
 * the network (status 0) or from a proxy that knows nothing about problem
 * details. Every component shows errors through this function, so all
 * three cases read the same way everywhere.
 */
export function describeHttpError(error: unknown): string {
  if (!(error instanceof HttpErrorResponse)) {
    return 'Something went wrong. Please try again.';
  }

  if (error.status === 0) {
    return 'Cannot reach the Sentinel API. Is it running on http://localhost:5080?';
  }

  if (error.status === 401) {
    return 'You are not signed in. Choose a user from the switcher at the top of the page.';
  }

  if (error.status === 403) {
    return 'You do not have permission to do that.';
  }

  const problem = error.error as { detail?: string; title?: string; errors?: Record<string, string[]> } | null;
  if (problem?.errors) {
    return Object.values(problem.errors).flat().join(' ');
  }

  return problem?.detail ?? problem?.title ?? `The server answered ${error.status} ${error.statusText}.`;
}

A failed HTTP call can be a network failure (status 0), an authentication problem, a validation problem with one message per field, or a proxy’s HTML error page. Every component shows errors through this function, so all of them read the same way.

15.5 Identity on every request

client/sentinel-web/src/app/core/http/demo-user.interceptor.ts 
import { HttpInterceptorFn } from '@angular/common/http';
import { inject } from '@angular/core';
import { Session } from '../session/session';

/** The header the API's development-only authentication scheme reads. */
export const DEMO_USER_HEADER = 'X-Demo-User';

/**
 * Adds the chosen demo user to every API request. In production this
 * interceptor would attach a bearer token instead; nothing else in the
 * application would change, because nothing else knows how identity travels.
 */
export const demoUserInterceptor: HttpInterceptorFn = (request, next) => {
  const email = inject(Session).signedInEmail();

  if (!email || !request.url.startsWith('/api/')) {
    return next(request);
  }

  return next(request.clone({ setHeaders: { [DEMO_USER_HEADER]: email } }));
};

A functional interceptor (HttpInterceptorFn) adds the header to calls to our own API only. The startsWith('/api/') check is the edge case: the identity must never leak to another origin, and there is a test for it.

15.6 The session

client/sentinel-web/src/app/core/session/session.ts 
import { HttpClient } from '@angular/common/http';
import { Injectable, computed, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { Observable, catchError, of, tap } from 'rxjs';
import { CurrentUser, DemoUser, NavigationNode } from '../models/api-models';

const STORAGE_KEY = 'sentinel.demoUser';

/**
 * Who is signed in, and what they may see. This is the one piece of state
 * shared across the whole application, so it lives in a root service and
 * is exposed as read-only signals. Components read it; only this class
 * writes it.
 */
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class Session {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);

  private readonly email = signal<string | null>(readStoredEmail());
  private readonly user = signal<CurrentUser | null>(null);
  private readonly menu = signal<NavigationNode[]>([]);

  /** The email sent in the demo header, or null when signed out. */
  readonly signedInEmail = this.email.asReadonly();
  readonly currentUser = this.user.asReadonly();
  readonly navigation = this.menu.asReadonly();
  readonly isSignedIn = computed(() => this.user() !== null);

  /**
   * The zone to show times in when a screen has no better information.
   * The user's profile zone, not the browser's: a Lagos user on a work
   * trip to London still thinks in Lagos time on their own account page.
   */
  readonly timeZone = computed(() => this.user()?.timeZoneId ?? 'UTC');

  getDemoUsers(): Observable<DemoUser[]> {
    return this.http.get<DemoUser[]>('/api/dev/demo-users');
  }

  /** Switches user (or signs out with null) and reloads everything that depends on identity. */
  signInAs(email: string | null): Observable<unknown> {
    this.email.set(email);
    writeStoredEmail(email);
    return this.refresh();
  }

  /** Reloads the profile and the menu for whoever is signed in now. */
  refresh(): Observable<unknown> {
    const email = this.email();
    this.loadNavigation().subscribe();

    if (!email) {
      this.user.set(null);
      return of(null);
    }

    return this.http.get<CurrentUser>('/api/me').pipe(
      tap((user) => this.user.set(user)),
      catchError(() => {
        // The stored user no longer exists (database reset). Fall back to
        // signed out rather than leaving a half-signed-in shell.
        this.email.set(null);
        writeStoredEmail(null);
        this.user.set(null);
        return of(null);
      }),
    );
  }

  private loadNavigation(): Observable<NavigationNode[]> {
    return this.http.get<NavigationNode[]>('/api/me/navigation').pipe(
      tap((nodes) => this.menu.set(nodes)),
      catchError(() => {
        this.menu.set([]);
        return of([]);
      }),
    );
  }
}

// localStorage can throw (private windows, disabled storage). A failure to
// remember the user must never stop the application from starting.
function readStoredEmail(): string | null {
  try {
    return localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function writeStoredEmail(email: string | null): void {
  try {
    if (email) {
      localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, email);
    } else {
      localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
    }
  } catch {
    // Nothing useful to do; the session still works for this tab.
  }
}

The one piece of application-wide state lives in a root service, exposed as read-only signals (asReadonly()). Components read; only Session writes. That is the interface-segregation principle in a front end, and it makes the fakes in tests tiny (Chapter 20).

localStorage access is wrapped in try/catch: it can throw in private windows and with storage disabled, and a failure to remember a user must never stop the application from starting.

15.7 Wiring it together

client/sentinel-web/src/app/app.config.ts 
import { provideHttpClient, withInterceptors } from '@angular/common/http';
import { ApplicationConfig, provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners } from '@angular/core';
import { provideRouter, withComponentInputBinding, withRouterConfig } from '@angular/router';
import { routes } from './app.routes';
import { demoUserInterceptor } from './core/http/demo-user.interceptor';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners(),
    provideHttpClient(withInterceptors([demoUserInterceptor])),
    provideRouter(
      routes,
      // Route data and query parameters arrive as component inputs, so a
      // page declares `readonly reason = input<string>()` instead of
      // injecting ActivatedRoute and subscribing.
      withComponentInputBinding(),
      withRouterConfig({ onSameUrlNavigation: 'reload' }),
    ),
  ],
};

withComponentInputBinding() lets route data and query parameters arrive as component inputs. onSameUrlNavigation: 'reload' lets the shell re-run the guard for the current page when you switch user (Chapter 16).

Chapter 16 · The Shell, Navigation and the Route Guard

This chapter connects the second scenario (page authorisation) to the front end: the menu shows only what the server says you may open, and the router refuses everything else.

16.1 The shell

client/sentinel-web/src/app/app.ts 
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { Router, RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router';
import { DemoUser } from './core/models/api-models';
import { Session } from './core/session/session';
import { NavTree } from './layout/nav-tree';
import { UserSwitcher } from './layout/user-switcher';

/** The shell: header, menu, and the outlet the pages render into. */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [RouterOutlet, NavTree, UserSwitcher],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <header class="top">
      <a class="brand" href="/">Sentinel</a>
      <app-user-switcher [users]="demoUsers()" [selected]="session.signedInEmail()" (selectedChange)="switchUser($event)" />
    </header>
    <div class="body">
      <nav aria-label="Main">
        <app-nav-tree [nodes]="session.navigation()" />
      </nav>
      <main>
        <router-outlet />
      </main>
    </div>
  `,
  styles: `
    :host { display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr; min-height: 100vh; }
    .top { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding: .6rem 1.25rem;
           background: var(--header-bg); color: var(--header-fg); }
    .brand { font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .04em; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; }
    .body { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 15rem 1fr; }
    nav { padding: 1rem .75rem; border-right: 1px solid var(--border); background: var(--surface); }
    main { padding: 1.25rem 1.75rem; }
    @media (max-width: 760px) { .body { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } nav { border-right: none; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); } }
  `,
})
export class App {
  protected readonly session = inject(Session);
  private readonly router = inject(Router);
  protected readonly demoUsers = signal<DemoUser[]>([]);

  constructor() {
    this.session.getDemoUsers().subscribe({
      next: (users) => this.demoUsers.set(users),
      error: () => this.demoUsers.set([]), // the API is down; pages will say so
    });
    this.session.refresh().subscribe();
  }

  protected switchUser(email: string | null): void {
    this.session.signInAs(email).subscribe(() => {
      // Re-run the guard for the page we are on: the new user may not be
      // allowed to see it. onSameUrlNavigation: 'reload' (app.config.ts)
      // and runGuardsAndResolvers: 'always' (app.routes.ts) make this work.
      this.router.navigateByUrl(this.router.url);
    });
  }
}

The shell owns two things: the list of demo users and the reaction to switching. It passes data down to two children and listens to one output. After a switch it re-navigates to the current URL, which, together with runGuardsAndResolvers: 'always' on the routes, re-runs the guard: the new user may not be allowed to stay where the old one was.

16.2 The user switcher: two-way binding by hand

client/sentinel-web/src/app/layout/user-switcher.ts 
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, input, output } from '@angular/core';
import { DemoUser } from '../core/models/api-models';

/**
 * A select box of demo users. It supports two-way binding:
 *
 *   <app-user-switcher [users]="users" [(selected)]="email" />
 *
 * `[(selected)]` is sugar for `[selected]="email" (selectedChange)="email = $event"`;
 * Angular wires it up because the output is named after the input plus
 * "Change". (Angular 17.2+ also offers `model()`, which declares both in one
 * line. The explicit pair is shown here because it is what every version of
 * Angular understands, including whatever version the test environment has.)
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-user-switcher',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <label>
      <span>Signed in as</span>
      <select [value]="selected() ?? ''" (change)="onChange($event)">
        <option value="">Nobody (signed out)</option>
        @for (user of users(); track user.email) {
          <option [value]="user.email" [selected]="user.email === selected()">
            {{ user.displayName }} · {{ user.description }}
          </option>
        }
      </select>
    </label>
  `,
  styles: `
    label { display: flex; gap: .5rem; align-items: center; font-size: .85rem; }
    select { max-width: 22rem; }
  `,
})
export class UserSwitcher {
  readonly users = input<DemoUser[]>([]);
  readonly selected = input<string | null>(null);
  readonly selectedChange = output<string | null>();

  protected onChange(event: Event): void {
    const value = (event.target as HTMLSelectElement).value;
    this.selectedChange.emit(value === '' ? null : value);
  }
}

The input selected and the output selectedChange form a pair that Angular recognises: a parent may write [(selected)]="email". The shell uses the long form, [selected] and (selectedChange), because it wants to do something on change, not just store the value.

16.3 The menu: a recursive component

client/sentinel-web/src/app/layout/nav-tree.ts 
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, input } from '@angular/core';
import { RouterLink, RouterLinkActive } from '@angular/router';
import { NavigationNode } from '../core/models/api-models';

/**
 * The menu, drawn from the server's navigation tree. Recursive: a node's
 * children are another <app-nav-tree>. The component has no idea who is
 * signed in or what they may see; the server already filtered the tree.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-nav-tree',
  // No need to import NavTree into itself: a standalone component can
  // always use its own selector, which is what makes recursion work.
  imports: [RouterLink, RouterLinkActive],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <ul [class.nested]="depth() > 0">
      @for (node of nodes(); track node.path) {
        <li>
          <a [routerLink]="node.path"
             routerLinkActive="active"
             [routerLinkActiveOptions]="{ exact: true }">{{ node.title }}</a>
          @if (node.children.length > 0) {
            <app-nav-tree [nodes]="node.children" [depth]="depth() + 1" />
          }
        </li>
      }
    </ul>
  `,
  styles: `
    ul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
    ul.nested { padding-left: .9rem; border-left: 1px solid var(--border); margin-left: .4rem; }
    a { display: block; padding: .3rem .5rem; border-radius: 4px; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; }
    a:hover { background: var(--hover); }
    a.active { background: var(--accent-bg); color: var(--accent); font-weight: 600; }
  `,
})
export class NavTree {
  readonly nodes = input.required<NavigationNode[]>();
  readonly depth = input(0);
}

The component renders itself for children. A standalone component can always use its own selector, so it does not list itself in imports. The depth input is passed down so the nested lists can be indented.

16.4 The routes

client/sentinel-web/src/app/app.routes.ts 
import { Route, Routes } from '@angular/router';
import { pageAccessGuard } from './core/access/page-access.guard';
import { DashboardPage } from './features/pages/dashboard-page';
import { ForbiddenPage } from './features/pages/forbidden-page';
import { PlaceholderPage } from './features/pages/placeholder-page';
import { AccountSecurityPage } from './features/security/account-security-page';

/**
 * Every route here has a page with the same path in the server's page tree,
 * and the guard asks the server about that path. Adding a route without
 * adding the page sends users to /forbidden ("Unknown"), which is the safe
 * failure: a page nobody configured is a page nobody may see.
 */
function guarded(path: string, route: Omit<Route, 'path'>): Route {
  return { path, canActivate: [pageAccessGuard], runGuardsAndResolvers: 'always', ...route };
}

function placeholder(path: string, title: string): Route {
  return guarded(path, { component: PlaceholderPage, data: { title } });
}

export const routes: Routes = [
  guarded('', { component: DashboardPage, pathMatch: 'full' }),
  placeholder('account', 'My account'),
  guarded('account/security', { component: AccountSecurityPage }),

  placeholder('reports', 'Reports'),
  placeholder('reports/finance', 'Finance'),
  placeholder('reports/finance/export', 'Ledger export'),
  placeholder('reports/operations', 'Operations'),
  placeholder('billing', 'Billing'),
  placeholder('support', 'Support desk'),

  // Admin screens are lazy: users who cannot open them never download them.
  placeholder('admin', 'Administration'),
  guarded('admin/users', { loadComponent: () => import('./features/admin/users-page').then((m) => m.UsersPage) }),
  guarded('admin/roles', { loadComponent: () => import('./features/admin/roles-page').then((m) => m.RolesPage) }),
  guarded('admin/access-explorer', {
    loadComponent: () => import('./features/admin/access-explorer-page').then((m) => m.AccessExplorerPage),
  }),

  placeholder('help', 'Help centre'),
  placeholder('status', 'System status'),

  { path: 'forbidden', component: ForbiddenPage },
  { path: '**', component: ForbiddenPage, data: { reason: 'Unknown' } },
];

Every route except /forbidden and the wildcard is guarded. The two helper functions are worth the lines: without them, twelve routes would repeat canActivate: [pageAccessGuard], runGuardsAndResolvers: 'always', and the thirteenth would forget it. The admin screens are lazy-loaded, so users who cannot open them never download them.

16.5 The guard

client/sentinel-web/src/app/core/access/page-access.guard.ts 
import { HttpClient } from '@angular/common/http';
import { inject } from '@angular/core';
import { CanActivateFn, Router } from '@angular/router';
import { Observable, catchError, map, of } from 'rxjs';
import { PageAccess } from '../models/api-models';

/**
 * Asks the API whether the signed-in user may open the page they are
 * navigating to, and sends them to /forbidden (with the reason) if not.
 *
 * Why ask the server on every navigation instead of checking the menu we
 * already have? Because the menu is only a *view* of the rules. A typed URL,
 * a bookmark or a stale tab must be judged by the rules themselves, and
 * the rules live in one place: PageAccessEvaluator, on the server.
 *
 * The guard protects the user experience, not the data. The API checks
 * permissions again on every data request, so a user who bypasses the
 * guard gets a blank page, never someone else's data.
 */
export const pageAccessGuard: CanActivateFn = (_route, state) => {
  const http = inject(HttpClient);
  const router = inject(Router);

  // The router's URL includes query string and fragment; pages are judged by path.
  const path = pathOnly(state.url);

  return http.get<PageAccess>('/api/me/page-access', { params: { path } }).pipe(
    map((verdict) =>
      verdict.isAllowed
        ? true
        : router.createUrlTree(['/forbidden'], { queryParams: { page: verdict.path, reason: verdict.reason } }),
    ),
    catchError((): Observable<boolean | ReturnType<Router['createUrlTree']>> =>
      // 404 (no such page) or the API is down. Fail closed: an unknown
      // page is not a reason to let someone in.
      of(router.createUrlTree(['/forbidden'], { queryParams: { page: path, reason: 'Unknown' } })),
    ),
  );
};

/** "/reports/finance?tab=2#top" -> "/reports/finance" */
export function pathOnly(url: string): string {
  const end = url.search(/[?#]/);
  const path = end === -1 ? url : url.slice(0, end);
  return path === '' ? '/' : path;
}

Why ask the server on every navigation instead of checking the menu the client already holds? Because the menu is a view of the rules, not the rules. A typed URL, a bookmark or a tab left open while an administrator revoked a role must all be judged by the rules themselves, and the rules live in one place.

And the guard is user experience, not security. The comment says so: the API checks permissions again on every data request, so a user who bypasses the guard (it is JavaScript running on their machine) gets an empty page, never someone else’s data.

Three edge cases are handled and tested:

  1. Denied → redirect to /forbidden with the page and the reason.
  2. Unknown page or API down → fail closed, reason Unknown.
  3. The router’s URL includes ?query and #fragment; access is decided by the path alone (pathOnly).

16.6 Explaining a denial

client/sentinel-web/src/app/core/access/access-reasons.ts 
import { AccessReason } from '../models/api-models';

/**
 * Plain-English explanations of the evaluator's reasons, for the people who
 * hit them. Written for a non-engineer: no "permission strings", no
 * "parents", just what happened and what to do next.
 */
const explanations: Record<AccessReason | 'Unknown', string> = {
  PublicPage: 'This page is open to everyone.',
  AuthenticatedUser: 'Every signed-in user can open this page.',
  PermissionGranted: 'One of your roles gives you access to this page.',
  NotAuthenticated: 'You need to sign in to see this page.',
  UserSuspended: 'Your account is suspended, so only public pages are available. Contact your administrator.',
  MissingPermission: 'None of your roles includes this page. Ask your administrator if you need it.',
  ExplicitlyDenied: 'Your administrator has specifically removed your access to this page.',
  ParentDenied: 'This page sits inside a section you do not have access to.',
  OrphanedPage: 'This page is misconfigured. Please report it to support.',
  CyclicHierarchy: 'This page is misconfigured. Please report it to support.',
  Unknown: 'This page does not exist, or we could not check your access to it right now.',
};

export function explainAccess(reason: string | null | undefined): string {
  return explanations[(reason ?? 'Unknown') as AccessReason] ?? explanations.Unknown;
}
client/sentinel-web/src/app/features/pages/forbidden-page.ts 
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, computed, input } from '@angular/core';
import { RouterLink } from '@angular/router';
import { explainAccess } from '../../core/access/access-reasons';

/**
 * Where the guard sends people it turns away. `page` and `reason` are query
 * parameters, bound to inputs by withComponentInputBinding().
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-forbidden-page',
  imports: [RouterLink],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <h1>You can't open this page</h1>
    @if (page()) {
      <p><code>{{ page() }}</code></p>
    }
    <p>{{ explanation() }}</p>
    <p><a routerLink="/">Back to the dashboard</a></p>
  `,
})
export class ForbiddenPage {
  readonly page = input<string>();
  readonly reason = input<string>();

  protected readonly explanation = computed(() => explainAccess(this.reason()));
}

These sentences are written for a non-engineer: no “permission strings”, no “parent nodes”. Writing them is the same skill as the customer reply in Chapter 24, and the same reviewer instinct applies: say what happened and what to do next.

client/sentinel-web/src/app/features/pages/placeholder-page.ts 
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, inject, input } from '@angular/core';
import { Session } from '../../core/session/session';

/**
 * Stands in for the screens this book does not build (reports, billing...).
 * They exist so the page tree and the guard have something real to protect.
 * `title` arrives from the route's `data` through component input binding.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-placeholder-page',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <h1>{{ title() }}</h1>
    <p>
      @if (session.currentUser(); as user) {
        {{ user.displayName }}, you can see this page because the access rules allow it.
      } @else {
        This page is public.
      }
    </p>
    <p class="muted">The real screen is out of scope for this book. Try the <em>Account security</em> page or the <em>Administration</em> section.</p>
  `,
  styles: `.muted { color: var(--muted); }`,
})
export class PlaceholderPage {
  protected readonly session = inject(Session);
  readonly title = input('Sentinel');
}

Chapter 17 · Passing Data Between Components: the Account Security Page

“How do you pass information between components?” is the first Angular-specific criterion on the scenario’s list. This chapter answers it with a real page, then lists every mechanism Angular offers and when each is the right one.

17.1 The component tree

AccountSecurityPage  (container: owns data, talks to the API, handles events)
 │
 ├── riskLevel, findingCount, assessedAtUtc, now ──▶ SecurityBanner
 │                                     ◀── (review) ─┘   "the user wants to see the findings"
 │
 ├── findings, timeZone, now, pendingKey ─────────▶ FindingList
 │                                ◀── (acknowledge) ─┘   emits the finding's key
 │
 └── signIns, timeZone ────────────────────────────▶ SignInTable

Data flows down through inputs. Intentions flow up through outputs. Only the container has side effects. If you remember one sentence from this part of the book, make it that one. It is what a reviewer is checking when they ask how you pass information, and it is what makes each child trivial to test and reuse: SecurityBanner appears on the dashboard and the admin explorer too, with a different reaction to (review) each time, and was never changed to allow it.

17.2 The presentational children

client/sentinel-web/src/app/features/security/risk.ts 
import { FindingKind, RiskLevel } from '../../core/models/api-models';

export type Tone = 'ok' | 'info' | 'warning' | 'danger';

export interface RiskPresentation {
  tone: Tone;
  headline: string;
  advice: string;
}

/**
 * What each risk level means to the person reading it. The words are the
 * product here: "High" tells a user nothing, "Someone may be using your
 * account" tells them to act.
 */
const presentations: Record<RiskLevel, RiskPresentation> = {
  None: {
    tone: 'ok',
    headline: 'No suspicious activity',
    advice: 'Your recent sign-ins all look like you.',
  },
  Low: {
    tone: 'info',
    headline: 'Something new to review',
    advice: 'We noticed a sign-in we have not seen before. If it was you, mark it so we stop asking.',
  },
  Medium: {
    tone: 'warning',
    headline: 'Your account may be at risk',
    advice: 'Review the activity below. If you do not recognise it, change your password now.',
  },
  High: {
    tone: 'danger',
    headline: 'Someone may be using your account',
    advice: 'Change your password now and sign out of all other sessions. Then review the activity below.',
  },
};

export function presentRisk(level: RiskLevel | null | undefined): RiskPresentation {
  // An unexpected value from a newer API is shown as the most cautious
  // known level rather than as "all clear". Fail towards telling the user.
  return presentations[level as RiskLevel] ?? presentations.Medium;
}

const findingTitles: Record<FindingKind, string> = {
  BruteForce: 'Repeated failed sign-ins',
  ImpossibleTravel: 'Sign-ins too far apart to be one person',
  NewCountry: 'Sign-in from a new country',
  NewDevice: 'Sign-in from a new device',
};

export function findingTitle(kind: FindingKind | string): string {
  return findingTitles[kind as FindingKind] ?? 'Unusual activity';
}

export function severityTone(level: RiskLevel | string): Tone {
  return presentRisk(level as RiskLevel).tone;
}

The words are the product. “High” tells a user nothing; “Someone may be using your account” tells them to act. Note the edge case: an unexpected level from a newer API is shown as a warning, never as all clear. When in doubt, fail towards telling the user.

client/sentinel-web/src/app/features/security/security-banner.ts 
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, computed, input, output } from '@angular/core';
import { RiskLevel } from '../../core/models/api-models';
import { RelativeTimePipe, UtcTimePipe } from '../../core/time/time-pipes';
import { presentRisk } from './risk';

/**
 * The verdict at the top of the page. Presentational: everything it shows
 * arrives through inputs, and the one thing it can do (ask to review)
 * leaves through an output. It does not know where the data came from or
 * what "review" will do, which is exactly what makes it reusable on the
 * admin screen and trivial to test.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-security-banner',
  imports: [RelativeTimePipe, UtcTimePipe],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <section class="banner" [class]="'tone-' + presentation().tone" role="status" aria-live="polite">
      <div class="banner-text">
        <h2>{{ presentation().headline }}</h2>
        <p>{{ presentation().advice }}</p>
        <p class="assessed" [title]="assessedAtUtc() | utcTime">
          Checked {{ assessedAtUtc() | relativeTime: now() }}
        </p>
      </div>
      @if (findingCount() > 0) {
        <button type="button" class="primary" (click)="review.emit()">
          Review {{ findingCount() }} {{ findingCount() === 1 ? 'item' : 'items' }}
        </button>
      }
    </section>
  `,
  styles: `
    .banner { display: flex; gap: 1rem; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between;
              padding: 1rem 1.25rem; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 6px solid; }
    .banner h2 { margin: 0 0 .25rem; font-size: 1.15rem; }
    .banner p { margin: .15rem 0; }
    .assessed { font-size: .8rem; opacity: .75; }
    .tone-ok { background: var(--ok-bg); border-color: var(--ok); }
    .tone-info { background: var(--info-bg); border-color: var(--info); }
    .tone-warning { background: var(--warning-bg); border-color: var(--warning); }
    .tone-danger { background: var(--danger-bg); border-color: var(--danger); }
  `,
})
export class SecurityBanner {
  readonly riskLevel = input.required<RiskLevel>();
  readonly findingCount = input(0);
  readonly assessedAtUtc = input.required<string>();
  readonly now = input.required<Date>();

  /** The user wants to see the findings. The parent decides what that means. */
  readonly review = output<void>();

  protected readonly presentation = computed(() => presentRisk(this.riskLevel()));
}
  • input.required<RiskLevel>(): the parent must bind it; forgetting is a compile error, not a blank banner.
  • input(0): optional, with a default.
  • output<void>(): an event with no payload. The banner does not know what “review” will do, and should not.
  • computed(...): derived state, recalculated only when riskLevel changes.
  • ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush: re-render only when an input or a signal it reads changes. With signal inputs this is the natural default.
  • role="status" and aria-live="polite": a screen reader announces the verdict when it changes.

import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, input, output } from '@angular/core';
import { SecurityFinding } from '../../core/models/api-models';
import { RelativeTimePipe, UtcTimePipe, ZonedDatePipe } from '../../core/time/time-pipes';
import { findingTitle, severityTone } from './risk';

/**
 * The findings, one card each, with a "This was me" button. Clicking it
 * does not call the API; it emits the finding's key and the page decides.
 * `pendingKey` comes back down as an input so the button can show progress
 * and refuse a double click while the request is in flight.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-finding-list',
  imports: [ZonedDatePipe, RelativeTimePipe, UtcTimePipe],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    @for (finding of findings(); track finding.key) {
      <article class="finding" [class]="'tone-' + tone(finding.severity)">
        <header>
          <span class="severity">{{ finding.severity }}</span>
          <h3>{{ title(finding.kind) }}</h3>
        </header>
        <p>{{ finding.summary }}</p>
        <p class="when">
          <time [attr.datetime]="finding.occurredAtUtc" [title]="finding.occurredAtUtc | utcTime">
            {{ finding.occurredAtUtc | zonedDate: timeZone() }}
          </time>
          · {{ finding.occurredAtUtc | relativeTime: now() }}
        </p>
        <div class="actions">
          <button type="button" (click)="acknowledge.emit(finding.key)" [disabled]="pendingKey() !== null">
            {{ pendingKey() === finding.key ? 'Saving…' : 'This was me' }}
          </button>
          <a href="/help">This wasn't me</a>
        </div>
      </article>
    } @empty {
      <p class="empty">Nothing to review.</p>
    }
  `,
  styles: `
    :host { display: grid; gap: .75rem; }
    .finding { border: 1px solid var(--border); border-left: 5px solid; border-radius: 6px; padding: .75rem 1rem; background: var(--surface); }
    .finding header { display: flex; gap: .5rem; align-items: baseline; }
    .finding h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; }
    .severity { font-size: .7rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .05em; }
    .when { font-size: .85rem; color: var(--muted); }
    .actions { display: flex; gap: 1rem; align-items: center; }
    .tone-info { border-left-color: var(--info); }
    .tone-warning { border-left-color: var(--warning); }
    .tone-danger { border-left-color: var(--danger); }
    .empty { color: var(--muted); }
  `,
})
export class FindingList {
  readonly findings = input.required<SecurityFinding[]>();
  readonly timeZone = input.required<string>();
  readonly now = input.required<Date>();
  readonly pendingKey = input<string | null>(null);

  readonly acknowledge = output<string>();

  protected readonly title = findingTitle;
  protected readonly tone = severityTone;
}

The list emits the key, not the whole finding and not an index. A key is stable; an index changes when the list does, which is how “I clicked This was me on one card and another one disappeared” bugs are born. track finding.key in the @for tells Angular the same thing about identity, so cards are not recreated on every reload.

pendingKey travels down after the event went up: the container decides that a request is in flight, and the child reflects it by disabling every button. That prevents double submission without the child knowing anything about HTTP.
